Adopting the mass and distance of $\mathrm{M87}^*$, we generate total-intensity synchrotron images and systematically explore the viewing inclination, disk thickness, and observing frequency. For the fiducial setup at $230\,\mathrm{GHz}$, raising $L/M$ from $0$ to $0.9$ contracts the critical curve diameter by $4.78\%$, shrinks the half-flux radius by $4.07\%$, and lowers the required electron-density scale by $9.15\%$. At $84\,\mathrm{GHz}$, the primary brightness peaks shift farther outside the critical curve due to enhanced synchrotron self-absorption, whereas the sharper emission rings at $230$ and $345\,\mathrm{GHz}$ closely trace the critical curve. Ultimately, we find that although the regular core systematically contracts the emission ring and alters the required plasma density, resolving these deviations from a Schwarzschild black hole demands angular resolution finer than that achievable with current baselines.

papers.title: Can torsion mimic a cosmological constant? A one-parameter logarithmic $f(T)$ extension of $Λ$CDM
papers.summary: We study a modified teleparallel gravity model of the $f(T)$ type. We propose a new functional form for in order to obtain a geometric origin to the $ΛCDM$ behavior in an appropriate limit. A perturbative expansion around the $ΛCDM$ regime is carried out, and the model's cosmic dynamics are calculated inside the flat FLRW background. By employing a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analysis using multiple observational datasets, such as Cosmic Chronometers, Type Ia Supernova compilations (DES-SN5YR, Pantheon+SH0ES, and Union 3.0), DESI DR2 BAO measurements, and Planck 2018 CMB distance priors, to constrain the model parameters. The findings show that the suggested $f(T)$ model accurately replicates the observed accelerated expansion and is statistically consistent with current cosmological observations. The model stays close to the $ΛCDM$ scenario while permitting tiny dynamical adjustments, as evidenced by the extra parameter $γ$, which quantifies deviations from the conventional cosmological model, being limited to values near zero.

papers.title: SHINE: Shear inference environment - Generative forward modelling for radio weak gravitational lensing
papers.summary: Next-generation radio interferometers, such as SKA, will observe the radio sky with unprecedented sensitivity and resolution enabling weak gravitational lensing studies using radio data, which not only complement optical observations but also probe higher redshifts. However, traditional shear estimation methods, based on measuring the ellipticity of observed galaxies, are not directly applicable to radio interferometric data. Interferometric observations are acquired in the Fourier domain, where galaxy images are delocalised, making shape measurements non-trivial. Furthermore, deconvolution methods such as CLEAN can introduce systematic errors when converting observations to the image domain, biasing shear estimates. To address these challenges, we propose a cosmic shear inference method based on forward generative modelling, which avoids explicit shape measurements. Our forward model simulates galaxy images, applies the shear transformation and, by including the instrumental response of the radio interferometer, simulates the visibilities of observed galaxies, with the likelihood explicitly defined in Fourier space. Using Monte Carlo sampling algorithms, we estimate the posterior distribution of the cosmic shear conditioned on a set of galaxy observations that share a common shear. We obtain unbiased shear estimates with sub-percent accuracy when applied to parametric galaxy simulations. We compare our method to state-of-the-art shear estimators, demonstrating a reduction in uncertainty of up to 3 times and no apparent multiplicative bias. We then show that applying this parametric model to COSMOS galaxies with realistic morphologies introduces a bias in the shear estimate over 10σ. Finally, we demonstrate that, by incorporating a generative forward model based on an autoencoder architecture trained on real galaxy images, we can mitigate this bias to below the 2σ level.

papers.title: Energy- and Time-Efficient Multi-Vehicle Trajectory Planning Using Augmented DAG Search in Configuration Space
papers.summary: Multi-vehicle trajectory planning for CAV requires balancing energy consumption and travel time while ensuring safety and scalability. While travel-time-optimal methods based on Integer Programming exhibit poor scalability in large-scale multi-vehicle scenarios, existing energy-oriented approaches fail to balance energy consumption and travel time. We extend a configuration-space framework for multi-vehicle trajectory planning to jointly locally optimize travel time and energy consumption. A weighted energy-travel time objective is combined with an efficient augmented DAG search on two-dimensional decompositions of a high-dimensional configuration space, enabling scalable and collision-free coordination of large numbers of vehicles. Although the proposed framework is applicable to other traffic scenarios, such as roundabouts and vehicle-following, we focus on intersections as a representative and challenging planning problem. To further improve performance for our methodology, we also extend the method with an insertion-ordering heuristic that exploits reduced-space geometric information. Combined with nonlinear model predictive control, the proposed framework is shown to scale to 40 vehicles, outperform MILP-based and convex optimization baselines in dense intersections, and reduce energy consumption at equalized travel times relative to time-optimal planning.
papers.comment: This manuscript is currently under review at IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems

papers.title: Experimental Investigation of Heat Transfer in Axisymmetric Open Cavities at Hypersonic Speeds
papers.summary: An experimental investigation was conducted to characterize the heat-transfer behavior of an axisymmetric cavity mounted on a cone with a semi-apex angle of $(48^ \circ)$ under Mach 6 freestream conditions in a Ludwieg tunnel. The effects of cavity geometry, represented by the length-to-depth ratio $(L/D = 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0,$ and $6.0)$, rear-wall height-to-depth ratio $(h/D = -0.25, 0,$ and $0.5)$, and Reynolds number ($Re_D = 23000 - 74000$) were systematically investigated. Flow-field characteristics and surface heat-transfer behavior were examined using schlieren and planar laser Rayleigh scattering visualization techniques, together with surface pressure and heat-transfer measurements. The results indicate that increasing the cavity length-to-depth ratio leads to a reduction in the downstream Stanton number $(St_d)$. For the longest cavity $L/D = 6$, however, the downstream Stanton number was found to exceed the upstream value $(St_u)$ indicating enhanced heat transfer in the region downstream of the cavity.
papers.comment: 12 Figures. The article is yet to be submitted to a journal

papers.title: Reading long-range information from a separable quantum record requires entangled measurements
papers.summary: Qubit probes record the relative orientation of neighboring, initially uncorrelated Ising spins through local interactions. Each probe encodes one bond label in two states with overlap $1-p$. The resulting probe record is fully separable. A receiver gets one copy and guesses whether two distant spins point in the same or opposite directions. On the square lattice, the best readout with separable measurement effects approaches success probability $1/2$ as the spin separation grows, for $0<p\le p_0=1-1/\sqrt2$. This includes all local operations with classical communication. The same conclusion holds for every measurement whose effects remain positive under partial transposition across every cut of the probes. For $p_*=0.29181\le p\le1$, a joint readout of the same record maintains a success probability above $1/2$ by a positive amount independent of distance. The overlap $[p_*,p_0]$ gives a strict separation between the readouts. A record that is created locally and contains no entanglement can therefore hold long-range information that only measurements with entangled effects can read.

papers.title: Tidal potential measured with distant optical clocks
papers.summary: Fibre-linked optical clocks sense tidal changes of the gravitational potential, but separating overlapping tidal components and quantifying their precision remain challenging. Using strontium and ytterbium clocks 692 km apart, we measure over 353 days a response of 0.95 (0.11) to the combined solid-Earth and ocean-loading tide and 1.01 (0.13) for the lunar semidiurnal group, and separate the lunar and solar-frequency semidiurnal contributions. A signal-to-noise model based on the actual sampling accounts for the lunar precision and guides future clock-network observations.

papers.title: Nanostructuring Semiconductor Surfaces Using Self-Assembled Metal Nanoparticles for Optoelectronic Applications
papers.summary: Semiconductor nanostructures are key light-management elements because their geometry can strengthen light-matter interaction, suppress reflection, and enhance optical coupling. Yet their adoption across material platforms is constrained by lithography, multistep pattern transfer, persistent masks, and material-specific etching. Here, we introduce a lithography-free two-step strategy in which thermally evaporated self-assembled Ga nanoparticles act as self-consuming masks during Ar inductively coupled plasma reactive-ion etching. Correlated transmission electron microscopy on GaAs reveals the formation mechanism. Comparable erosion of the Ga nanoparticles and exposed substrate progressively converts Ga-capped pedestals into pure semiconductor nanocones while preserving crystalline order. Nanocone dimensions extend from tens to hundreds of nanometres, and surface coverage is tunable through Ga deposition and plasma power. The same process produces nanocones on GaP and Si and dense nanostructures on polycrystalline hybrid metal-halide perovskite without detectable PbI2 formation. During nanostructuring, the sun-weighted reflectance reaches minima of 11-15% on the monocrystalline substrates, whereas the perovskite achieves 0.5% after complete mask consumption. The approach therefore combines a self-assembled mask, its consumption, and pattern transfer in a single physical etching step, providing a simple route to light-coupling surfaces for III-V, Si, and perovskite optoelectronics.

papers.title: Nonreciprocal Josephson Dynamics of a $\mathcal{PT}$-Symmetric Atomtronic SQUID
papers.summary: We investigate non-Hermitian Josephson dynamics in an atomtronic quantum interference device (AQUID), formed by a ring Bose Einstein condensate with balanced atomic gain and loss regions and two moving optical barriers. The balanced gain and loss profile establishes a parity time symmetric potential while breaking spatial inversion symmetry, providing the essential ingredients for nonreciprocal Josephson transport. The dynamics are monitored nondestructively through the phase quadrature spectrum of an optomechanical cavity driven by Laguerre Gaussian beams coupled to the condensate. We demonstrate that increasing the local gain and loss strength softens the parity time symmetric collective mode towards an exceptional point, as verified by Bogoliubov de Gennes analysis. The associated coherent population exchange produces an additional characteristic splitting in the cavity output spectrum. For linearly translating barriers, non-Hermiticity provides an additional control parameter for tuning the critical current. When the barriers undergo simultaneous translation and rotation, the rotation induced phase modifies the interference between counter propagating currents, offering further control over the nonreciprocal response. Under periodic barrier modulation, we find more pronounced Shapiro steps in the current voltage characteristics due to the intrinsic parity time symmetric collective mode. Finally, we propose an alternative Hermitian realization using a tilted optical lattice, providing an experimentally accessible route to engineering biased transport and population transfer. Our results establish parity time symmetric atomtronic SQUIDs as a versatile platform for controlling nonreciprocal Josephson transport and collective excitations in driven quantum fluids.

papers.title: ANTIOCH-VS: From Sequence to Hits with Modular, Open-Source Ensemble Virtual Screening
papers.summary: Structure-based virtual screening needs a receptor conformation that fits the ligand class, but for most targets no ligand-bound crystal is available -- and a single predicted model or an apo structure often misses the binding-competent state. We present ANTIOCH-VS, an open-source framework that runs an entire in silico screening campaign, from a protein sequence to a ranked shortlist of candidate binders, as one plug-and-play workflow. It first builds a conformational ensemble by reduced-MSA subsampling with ColabFold, then uses AlphaFold2-RAVE (AF2RAVE) -- short molecular-dynamics simulations with State Predictive Information Bottleneck analysis -- to pick out docking-ready, Boltzmann-weighted metastable states. It then detects the binding pocket, prepares receptors and ligands, docks the library across the ensemble with DOCK6 or AutoDock Vina, builds a consensus ranking, and triages the top hits by physics-based metadynamics (CTMD). We benchmark it on two very different targets, JAK2 kinase and ADRB2 GPCR, using their DUD-E benchmark sets of known binders and property-matched decoys. Starting from sequence alone -- no ligand-bound crystal, no manual intervention -- the AF2RAVE ensembles gave top-20 shortlists strongly enriched for true binders: a 20% hit rate for JAK2 and 60% for ADRB2 (random ~1-2%), on par with ligand-bound crystals and, for the kinase, above single AF2 models and an apo crystal. The full pipeline runs end to end on a workstation or HPC from a single command, or each module can be run on its own with user-supplied inputs. ANTIOCH-VS is freely available at https://github.com/tiwarylab/antioch-vs
papers.comment: 34 pages, 19 figures (6 main text, 13 supplementary); code available at https://github.com/tiwarylab/antioch-vs

papers.title: ForeseeDrive: Future-Token Conditioning for Anticipatory Generative Driving
papers.summary: Generative driving planners can represent diverse ego futures, but a downstream scorer can choose only among sampled candidates; it cannot recover an absent maneuver. We present ForeseeDrive, which turns future scene evolution into a deployable interface for shaping candidate generation. Rather than reconstructing dense future states or scoring a fixed menu, ForeseeDrive derives query-indexed tokens from logged actor motion, occupancy evolution, route interactions, and TTC margins, and predicts the same token space from present context at deployment. The tokens condition trajectory geometry before candidates materialize. A zero-token-gated residual path and candidate-preservation loss limit unnecessary drift, while a TTC-margin guard targets brittle safe-to-unsafe boundary crossings. Under their respective benchmark protocols, ForeseeDrive reaches 89.2 PDMS on NAVSIM navtest, 0.41\,m average L2 and 0.05\% collision rate on nuScenes validation, and a 76.50 driving score on Bench2Drive. Controlled DiffusionDrive/NAVSIM diagnostics show an exact zero-token no-op, a small aligned-over-shuffled selected-PDM advantage under preservation, mixed oracle-best quality, and localized TTC-boundary failures. Together, the benchmark results and bounded mechanism tests support future-conditioned generation as a practical interface for anticipation. Code is included in the supplementary materials.
papers.comment: 15 pages (8 pages main text + appendix), 3 figures, 7 tables

papers.title: LM-SimBench: A Unified Framework, Dataset, and Benchmark for Large Language Model Training Simulation
papers.summary: Evaluating candidate parallelization strategies through distributed training runs makes strategy selection prohibitively expensive at scale. Performance simulation offers a lower cost alternative, yet controlled comparisons among existing simulators remain difficult because they differ in the training stages they model and the workloads on which they are evaluated. We introduce LM-SimBench, a unified framework, profiling dataset, and benchmark for evaluating LLM training simulators. The framework decomposes simulation into functional stages from model compilation to schedule level aggregation, connecting execution representations and cost estimators to measurable evaluation targets. Following this framework, we profile 23 model settings from 10 dense and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLM families on an Ascend Neural Processing Unit (NPU) cluster. The resulting dataset contains 348 feasible configurations that jointly vary five parallelism dimensions and activation recomputation, with six views spanning configuration, rank, operator, event, and kernel granularity. Evaluations of representative training simulators demonstrate how LM-SimBench supports comparisons of prediction accuracy, assessment of configuration selection, and diagnosis of prediction errors. Matched GPU-NPU experiments validate the cross-platform applicability of the collection and evaluation protocol and demonstrate NPU-guided GPU configuration selection.

papers.title: Ninety-Six Ways to Measure a Scribe: Fragmented Evaluation of Ambient Scribes in Healthcare
papers.summary: Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribes have moved rapidly from experimental pilots to enterprise-wide deployment across health systems, promising reduced documentation burden and improved clinician experience. While research evaluating these tools has expanded quickly, there are no agreed-upon protocols or standardized metrics for assessing their performance, making it difficult to compare findings or cumulatively synthesize evidence across studies. Across 54 recent evaluation studies, we identify ten evaluation dimensions and 40 distinct metrics, operationalized in 96 different ways-35 of them (36%) used by only a single study. Assessment is dominated by documentation efficiency and time, measured in 44 of 54 studies. The other dimensions appear at broadly similar rates (16-24 studies each), and safety and clinical outcome least consistently of all. Ripple effects on the broader care system, such as impact on patients' care outcomes, redistribution of work, changes in billing and coding intensity, and downstream use of notes by other clinicians are rarely assessed. Moreover, the metrics used rely heavily on self-report and are fragmented and inconsistently operationalized, which limits comparability and hinders synthesis across studies. As an effort to support more rigorous and cumulative evaluation, in this paper we review the study designs, data sources, and metrics commonly used to evaluate ambient AI scribes in healthcare settings, discuss the limitations of current evaluation practice, and argue for a more holistic approach grounded in a standardized, multi-dimensional set of metrics.

papers.title: UniFlow-RS: Unified Generative Prediction for Heterogeneous Remote-Sensing Tasks
papers.summary: Remote-sensing foundation models increasingly unify representations across sensing modalities and downstream tasks, yet their prediction mechanisms remain largely task-specific. Separate decoders, prediction heads, and objectives leave prediction fragmented across tasks. This naturally raises a question: can heterogeneous remote-sensing tasks share the prediction process? UniFlow-RS answers this question with a single latent flow-matching predictor shared across tasks. This requires addressing two key challenges: unifying heterogeneous prediction spaces and harmonizing joint optimization across tasks. First, we cast heterogeneous task outputs into structured visual targets in a common latent space, allowing them to be modeled by the same pretrained flow predictor. Task-dependent conditioning further accommodates differences in input configurations. Second, we optimize all tasks with a common Flow Matching objective, eliminating task-specific prediction losses. To mitigate optimization mismatch across tasks and modalities, we introduce Task-Modality Adaptive Timestep Sampling (TMAS), which dynamically allocates training timesteps according to the online learning state of each task-modality group. Using a single shared model, UniFlow-RS handles six tasks and thirteen datasets, surpassing recent task-specific state-of-the-art methods on several benchmarks while remaining competitive on the others. Beyond these benchmarks, the same checkpoint demonstrates strong zero-shot transfer across unseen datasets, task settings, occlusion conditions, and near-infrared false-color imagery, without target-specific adaptation.

papers.title: DustER: Dust Extinction with Photometric Red Galaxies
papers.summary: We present DustER, a new method for reconstructing dust reddening maps from photometric galaxy survey data. DustER uses red galaxies as "standard crayons". That is, it relies on the mean color of red-sequence galaxies being independent of their position in the sky. Given the galaxy's redshift, the difference between a galaxy's observed color and its expected color measures the reddening by dust along the galaxy's line of sight. When using photometric galaxy survey data, the method must rely on photometric redshifts, which, combined with selection effects, bias the recovered dust maps. DustER uses a novel approach to characterize and correct for these biases by leveraging the known statistical properties of the distribution of dust around the Milky Way. Testing on simulations, we find that the recovered dust maps are contaminated by large-scale structure. However, when we use the DustER map to deredden and select red-sequence galaxies, we find the resulting two-point function is not contaminated by dust.
papers.comment: 27 pages, 9 figures, 6 tables, prepared for submission to JCAP

papers.title: AutoThreshold: Joint Confusion-Profile Learning for Adaptive Mask Binarization
papers.summary: A single validation-tuned threshold can become brittle when dense-score distributions shift. We introduce AutoThreshold, a post-hoc policy that predicts the joint mass of positive and negative pixels over score bins. This target directly parameterizes threshold-indexed confusion counts, avoiding products of independently estimated prevalence and class-conditional rates. Softmax normalization and cumulative decoding yield coherent, monotone confusion profiles; a plug-in decoder then selects a threshold for any $F_β$ objective without retraining the head. Across three independently trained Kvasir pipelines transferred to four polyp datasets, Joint exceeds continuous Otsu by $0.0080 \pm 0.0046$ external macro Dice, with positive gains in 3/3 runs. On the reference pipeline, three head seeds achieve $0.6324 \pm 0.0027$, 0.0085 above Otsu; direct-utility Ridge achieves 0.6342, with the paired difference interval spanning zero. The same Joint checkpoints outperform Otsu for $F_{0.5}$, Dice, and $F_2$. On developmental KITTI Road leave-one-corruption-family-out evaluation, Joint improves over scalar regression by 0.0082 [0.0064, 0.0101], while direct utility is 0.0022 higher. These results establish joint confusion prediction as a useful, metric-retargetable inductive bias, without claiming Bayes-optimal $F_β$ decisions.

papers.title: Shot noise, aperture and resolution in Fourier measurements of disc lopsidedness: TNG50-1 and TNG100-1 analysed with TNGGalaxyLab
papers.summary: We present TNGGalaxyLab, an open-source Python pipeline for particle-based Fourier decomposition of the stellar surface density of simulated disc galaxies. It measures m = 1-4 amplitude and phase profiles in the Rix and Zaritsky (1995) normalisation, handles IllustrisTNG snapshot conventions, and recovers injected amplitudes in synthetic discs to better than 2 per cent at N = 5 x 10^5. Fourier amplitudes are positive-definite, so Poisson noise biases them upwards by an amount that grows as the particle number falls. We measure a per-galaxy noise floor by randomising particle azimuths and define a noise-corrected amplitude A1,corr. Downsampling TNG50-1 discs to the TNG100-1 particle mass inflates the uncorrected A1 by 40-60 per cent, while A1,corr is recovered to within approximately 10 per cent. We then process all central galaxies with 3.16 x 10^9 < M*/Msun < 10^11 in TNG50-1 (915) and TNG100-1 (6717) with identical settings in the [1.5, 2.5] Rd aperture. Removing the bootstrap and shot-noise biases lowers the TNG100/TNG50 ratio of median A1 from 2.3 to 1.6. At fixed stellar mass, kinematically selected TNG100-1 discs remain 1.5-1.9 times more lopsided after correction; this excess persists whether the aperture is defined in Rd or in kpc, is not explained by kappa_rot or D/T, and is largest at 3.5-6 kpc. TNG50-1 is statistically consistent with the mass-matched S4G sample of Zaritsky et al. (2013); TNG100-1 is not. The low A1 reported for TNG100 by Lokas (2022) cannot be read as a resolution deficit, since with matched measurements TNG100-1 is more lopsided than TNG50-1. Code and catalogues are public.
papers.comment: 1 pages, 10 figures. The TNGGalaxyLab Python pipeline and catalogues are publicly available

papers.title: Direct numerical simulation of turbulent heat transfer in water with temperature-dependent viscosity and conductivity
papers.summary: We study turbulent forced convection of liquid water in a plane channel by direct numerical simulation (DNS), with temperature-dependent viscosity and thermal conductivity. The simulations cover wall heating and cooling, mean-to-wall temperature ratios from 0.83 to 1.3, wall temperatures from 277 to 360\,K and wall Prandtl numbers from 2 to 12. Compared with constant-property flow at the same bulk Reynolds number, the friction coefficient changes by $-39\,\%$ to $+32\,\%$, the heat transfer coefficient referred to the wall Prandtl number changes by up to a factor of $2.3$, and empirical correlations deviate from the DNS by up to $26\,\%$. Instantaneous fields and spectra show that the wall friction Reynolds number misrepresents the range of turbulent scales, whereas near-wall streaks of velocity and temperature have a common spacing when scaled with the local viscous length. The density is constant, so the mean velocity and temperature defects in the core follow those of constant-property flow. To predict friction and heat transfer, we map the mean profiles onto those of constant-property flow through integral transformations derived from the mean momentum and energy balances, with empirical corrections of the eddy viscosity and diffusivity calibrated on the DNS. This approach, developed for air, is extended to liquids, whose conductivity is not proportional to the viscosity and whose Prandtl number varies across the channel. The inverse transformations predict friction and heat transfer within $2\,\%$ of the DNS, except at the lowest Reynolds numbers. The same corrections, introduced in the Spalart--Allmaras model, halve its friction error.

papers.title: From Prediction to Action: Learning Physical Context for Deformable Linear Object Manipulation
papers.summary: A representation that accurately predicts a deformable object's response is not necessarily the one most useful for choosing manipulation actions. We study this distinction between predictive utility and decision utility in planar single-grasp shape control of Deformable Linear Objects (DLOs). As a common decision backbone, we introduce Geometry-Pointer-Flow (GPF), a geometry-grounded policy that separates grasp-location selection from grasp-conditioned motion generation. Its geometry-only variant reduces one-step executed shape error by 32.8% relative to a DLO-specific diffusion policy, while using 18.7 times fewer parameters and achieving approximately 193 times faster inference. On this backbone, we compare physical context represented by ground-truth parameters, estimated parameters, and learned interaction-history representations, for both forward prediction and executed control. For prediction, ground-truth physical parameters reduce next-shape error by 15.8% over geometry alone, and estimated parameters are slightly more predictive than interaction history. This ordering does not carry over to control: estimated parameters provide no detectable one-step control gain, whereas history-conditioned GPF reduces executed error by 9.9% relative to geometry-only GPF across 470 paired simulation trials. In closed loop, interaction history improves strict-threshold attainment in simulation and yields the strongest zero-shot performance on hardware. All policies are trained exclusively in simulation and transferred to the physical robot without real-world training or fine-tuning. These results show that physical context should be evaluated by the decisions it supports rather than by predictive accuracy alone. Code will be released upon acceptance.

papers.title: Edge quantum weight of finite Chern flakes and its topological floor
papers.summary: The zero-point energy of a circuit measures the polarization fluctuation of an insulator coupled to it. In a crystal this is the bulk quantum weight $K_\mathrm{bulk}$, which the Chern number $C$ bounds below by $|C|$. We show that a finite Chern flake adds an edge term that survives as the flake grows. The low-frequency transitions of its chiral edge carry a dipole weight, the sum of their squared dipole matrix elements, $K_\mathrm{edge}\geq|C|$ per unit area, a floor that follows from the positive absorption of both circular polarizations by every transition and the known cancellation of circular dichroism between edge and bulk. A weakly coupled circuit slower than the edge modes therefore reads $K_\mathrm{bulk}+K_\mathrm{edge}$, averaged over two field directions, while a faster one below the bulk gap approaches $K_\mathrm{bulk}$, so which quantum weight is measured depends on whether the flake is made large or the circuit slow first. Exact free-fermion calculations on lattice flakes bear out the floor and this dependence on the circuit frequency. The result holds at weak coupling, which a growing flake at fixed coupling eventually leaves. Above the floor, the edge weight of one channel is a number fixed by the shape of the boundary and the edge velocities, which square and rectangular lattice flakes follow to within 0.003. Each further edge channel adds its own such number, while the circular dichroism of the edge counts only the net chirality.
papers.comment: 39 pages, 13 figures. Data and code: doi:10.5281/zenodo.24112974

papers.title: Reducing Massive Scattering Amplitudes to Normal Form
papers.summary: Local amplitude reduction is a crucial tool in effective field theory (EFT) calculations. While polynomial normal forms reproduce the massless y-basis, massive amplitudes require reduction rules that preserve little-group tensor contractions. We generalize Gröbner-basis reduction to covariant tensor identities, determining leading monomials in their contraction contexts and generating the higher-degree rules induced by mass determinants. Using three-, four-, and five-point replacement catalogs, we demonstrate symbolic-mass amplitude reductions and reproduce the independent three- and four-vector operator bases, providing traceable normal-form reductions for local EFT matching and syzygy analysis.
papers.comment: 7 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables, Code and rule catalogs available at https://github.com/XiaoMing-lei/MassiveAmplitudeReduction

papers.title: Towards a new model of the compact triple system $λ$ Tauri I. Improved periods and preliminary elements of the triple system
papers.summary: We analysed our new radial velocity measurements and photometric observations (covering a time interval of 46838~days and 39100~days, respectively) as well as those from previous studies to derive accurate ephemerides for both orbits of the compact triple system $λ$ Tau. In the case of the inner eclipsing subsystem, we obtained a~linear ephemeris of T min.I=HJD 2440998.86069(35)+3.952952845(81)xE, improving the accuracy of the previous solutions by more than an order of magnitude. This allowed us to reproduce well all available light curve minima, including the first one recorded in 1844. Furthermore, the period of the outer subsystem, determined from radial velocity analysis, appears to be constant over the interval of available observations, with the corresponding linear ephemeris being T periast.=HJD 2456822.5(3.6)+33.02480(28)xE. Assuming near coplanarity of the inner and outer orbits, we estimated the preliminary physical properties of the whole system. We found that the secondary of the inner subsystem is filling or nearly filling its Roche lobe. We used the long-term stability of the eclipsing subsystem period to place a strong upper limit on the rate of the proposed episodic mass transfer to its primary component. Our results constitute a preparatory step for a follow-up study that will also include an analysis of a rich collection of optical spectro-interferometric observations and use a full-fledged numerical model to describe the evolution of the orbital architecture of the system. Particular attention will be focused on determining the inner orbit forced eccentricity and understanding the absence of the apsidal advance of the outer orbit in our present solution.
papers.comment: 12 pages, 9 figures; accepted for publication in Astronomy and Astrophysics

papers.title: Achieving Robust Channel Estimation Neural Networks on Doppler effects by Designed Training Data
papers.summary: Channel estimation is crucial in wireless communication systems. Many existing works train and test their models using the same or similar channel. However, practical channels are infinitely diverse and time-variant while data-driven algorithms often degrade on new and previously unseen channels. This prohibits the practical implementation of neural networks for channel estimation, particularly in high speed scenarios characterized by rapidly channel profile changes and very high Doppler shifts. Online training can fine-tune models to adapt to new channels, but requires high computation resource and incurs significant latency for physical-layer devices. Moreover, online training cannot exhaustively cover all possible channels because there are infinitely many possible channels. Therefore, we investigate the ability of neural networks to generalize to wireless channels. This paper proposes design criteria to generate synthetic training data, which guaranty that the resulting networks perform robustly across wireless channels, especially for very high Doppler shifts and different Doppler spectra. It ensures that offline-trained neural networks require no prior information or online training to precisely estimate the new channels. To demonstrate general applicability, we use neural networks with different levels of complexity to show that the generalization achieved appears to be independent of architecture. From simulation results, neural networks achieve a certain performance across wireless channels with different unseen power delay profiles (PDP) and Doppler shifts.

papers.title: Physics-Constrained Autoencoder for Interpretable Health Representation Learning in Turbofan Engines
papers.summary: Health Indices (HIs) summarize degradation from operational data and support diagnostic and prognostic tasks in Prognostics and Health Management (PHM). Their usefulness depends on capturing degradation and interpreting system condition. Autoencoders learn such representations from unlabelled monitoring data; however, when training is driven only by reconstruction, the physical meaning of latent variables remains undefined, limiting their interpretation and diagnostic value. This work proposes a physics-constrained autoencoder that embeds system knowledge as an inductive bias in the decoder architecture and as a learning bias in the loss function. The decoder contains differentiable physical equations that receive latent variables and operating conditions as inputs, structurally guiding each latent variable to represent a predefined physical quantity and enabling component-level analysis before aggregation into a system-level HI.The methodology is benchmarked on the N-CMAPSS dataset against alternative representations. Reconstruction reaches an $R^2$ of 0.9993 and an MAE of 0.0036, comparable to fully data-driven models. After operating-condition correction, the inferred physical quantities track degradation, and their aggregation produces an HI with a Spearman correlation of 0.9791 with the ground truth, an RMSE of 0.0286, and an MAE of 0.0233. The methodology is further evaluated using a single model trained across four datasets representing distinct degradation scenarios. This model preserves component-level signatures that distinguish compression-side from expansion-side degradation without diagnostic labels.Finally, the proposed framework enables degradation trends to be visualized on component maps, providing a health representation in a form familiar to engine operators and domain experts.

papers.title: Chain of Physics: Supporting Fault Diagnosis with Engineering-Inspired Large Language Model Reasoning
papers.summary: Fault diagnosis in complex systems requires linking observed changes in physical quantities to the failure mechanisms that produce them. Experienced engineers perform this task by combining sensor information with knowledge of system behavior and fault propagation. Large Language Models (LLMs) can support this process, but their diagnostic reasoning depends on the availability of asset-specific engineering knowledge and on how this knowledge is represented and used during inference. This work introduces Chain of Physics (CoP), an LLM-based fault-diagnosis framework built around a Constrained Knowledge Graph (CKG) generated automatically from asset-specific reference documentation. CoP addresses failure-sensor association from textual engineering knowledge. The CKG stores diagnostic chains connecting failure modes, changes in physical quantities, and monitoring sensors. During inference, semantically similar graph paths are retrieved for each question and used as both information and in-context examples for the reasoning process. Candidate failure modes are extracted from the question and analysed independently through dedicated LLM calls, which generate plausible failure-to-observation chains. A final decision module compares these chains with the available answer choices. CoP is evaluated on the FailureSensorIQ benchmark across four industrial asset classes and three LLMs. Compared with direct prompting and conventional Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), CoP improves diagnostic accuracy across all evaluated models, with gains ranging from 7.8 to 19.6 percentage points and from 11.7 to 18.2 percentage points, respectively. The results show that structured engineering knowledge can improve LLM-based diagnostic reasoning when graph retrieval is combined with in-context examples of fault propagation.

papers.title: Recurrent Modular Structure in Spiking Neural Network Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Biological neural circuits are both modular and recurrent, with dense communities sparsely linked to one another. Spiking neural networks (SNNs) for reinforcement learning are usually feed-forward, and it is unclear how to obtain functional modules in a recurrent SNN or what they buy. In this work, we introduce a class of spiking networks, called Community Recurrent SNNs (CoRe SNNs): recurrent networks partitioned into communities with fixed roles. A controller community receives the stimulus, each action has its own community, and latent communities carry internal state. Spiking activity is then a walk between communities, and the action is the community the walk reaches. All learning is local and three-factor, and the recurrent communities are closer to cortical microcircuits than a feed-forward actor. We compare three regimes for obtaining the communities: dynamic modularity, in which a new learning rule we introduce, Map-STDP, encourages modular structure during learning; partial modularity, in which a stochastic block model (SBM) initialization enforces it partly; and full modularity, in which sealing enforces it fully. On CartPole, across three spiking neuron models, Map-STDP improves learning over the same network without it matches full modularity (sealed communities) on two of the three models, and makes the observed spike walk more compressible. Replacing the feed-forward actor of a TD-STDP actor-critic with recurrent action communities improves on the feed-forward network on CartPole and LunarLander, and matches it on Acrobot. How strongly to enforce modularity depends on the task: full modularity helps most on Acrobot, while on LunarLander the dynamic, partial and full regimes perform alike. Overall, these recurrent modular networks can match or even improve upon feed-forward approaches, with improvements in bio-plausibility and energy efficiency.

papers.title: Memory-gated transient anomalous transport of quasiparticles out of equilibrium
papers.summary: Anomalous transport is ubiquitous across condensed matter, materials science, and biophysics. Yet, in far-from-equilibrium settings, what determines when, how much, and in which direction transport departs from diffusion remains a fundamental open question. By adopting the dispersive Holstein model of small polarons as representative of a wide class of dissipative systems, we show that a signed bath memory time governs the direction and the strength of the transient departure, and that when it vanishes, diffusion emerges without an asymptotic delay. Tuning the dissipative environment from resonant to off-resonant with the carrier density of states, transport turns from subdiffusion to superdiffusion as the memory time changes sign. Microscopically, we trace this memory effect to a competition between polaron formation and coherent polaron motion. These findings establish a unified memory-based description of transient anomalous transport, offering a path to control nonequilibrium quasiparticle flow through environmental tuning.

papers.title: Lilo: A Multi-Agent Conversational Sandbox for Children's Digital Communication
papers.summary: Children's peer conflicts increasingly play out in group chats, where tone and timing are stripped away, and a hurtful message is easier to send than to say aloud. We present Lilo, a multi-agent conversational system that lets children practice such conversations, so they are better prepared when they encounter them in real digital communication. In Lilo, the child joins two AI-driven peers mid-argument, coached by a mentor character, also named Lilo, through a Stop-Think-Act traffic light. Through an exploratory study with 28 children (aged 9-11), we examine how children engage with Lilo's simulated peer conflict and the mentor's traffic-light interventions. The study included an intervention with Lilo, surveys before and after the intervention, and exit interviews. Participants reported significantly higher self-efficacy for coping with unpleasant messages after their interaction with Lilo. They felt safe experimenting, knowing nothing they wrote would be held against them.

papers.title: Concentration-Based Probabilistic Reachability for Linear Systems under Multiplicative Uncertainty and Additive Noise
papers.summary: This paper investigates probabilistic reachability for discrete-time linear stochastic systems subject to bounded multiplicative uncertainty and potentially unbounded additive noise. To address the conservatism of reachable sets constructed solely from covariance information, we develop two complementary approaches based on sub-Gaussian and sub-exponential matrix moment-generating-function characterizations. The sub-Gaussian approach relies on a worst-case envelope over the uncertainty support, whereas the sub-exponential approach exploits expectation-based propagation of the matrix variance proxy. Both approaches are used to construct probabilistic reachable sets with explicit probability guarantees, considering ellipsoidal confidence regions and half-space bounds. For the latter, we derive a necessary and sufficient condition under which the sub-exponential chance-constraint margin is no larger than its sub-Gaussian counterpart. Numerical results show that the proposed bounds can be less conservative than those based on the covariance, and illustrate the complementary nature of the two approaches across probability levels.

papers.title: Elastic-WAM: Adaptive Spatiotemporal Imagination for Efficient Robot Control
papers.summary: World-Action Models improve robot control by predicting future visual dynamics, but iterative video denoising incurs substantial inference overhead. Recent approaches reduce this cost through partial future denoising, yet typically rely on fixed refinement budgets. Our empirical observations reveal that preferred refinement depths vary across tasks and states, while different future regions exhibit varying relevance to action generation. Motivated by these findings, we propose Elastic-WAM, which adaptively allocates world refinement computation across temporal denoising time and spatial future space. A unified spatiotemporal refinement demand field governs when to stop world refinement, how far to advance each denoising step, and which regions to refresh. We parameterize this field with a shared temporal basis and spatial amplitudes, and learn it through a three-stage action-grounded supervised procedure. At inference, the learned field guides recurrent sparse world refinement to improve task success while reducing inference overhead. Evaluations across diverse simulation benchmarks and real-world long-horizon manipulation demonstrate state-of-the-art control performance with reduced inference latency.

papers.title: A Cross-Scenario Survey and Analysis of Self-Evolving Multimodal Agents
papers.summary: Recent work shows that multimodal agents increasingly self-improve without recurring human annotation. However, each self-improvement mechanism is designed and evaluated within a single scenario, leaving its preconditions unverified under cross-scenario transfer. This survey investigates the structural source of asymmetric mechanism transfer across four scenarios: multimodal reasoning, multimodal generation, GUI and Web navigation, and embodied manipulation. We first formalize the self-evolving multimodal agent by four criteria and a differentia of self-reference, and adopt the three-stage self-evolving loop of experience generation, feedback acquisition, and update consolidation as our analytical framework to position the scenarios along ceilings on rollout count and feedback fidelity. Comparing self-evolving with fixed loops within each scenario separates the limitations that the scenario imposes from those inherent in the self-evolving design. We then recast each mechanism as a trade-off that raises a scarce factor by presupposing a task-structural resource, such as output equivalence or checkable outcomes, and judge it portable, conditional, blocked, or redundant across scenarios. We attribute the asymmetry to divergent combinations of scarce factors and resources across opposite transfer directions, and identify the matched-budget measurements that could overturn these still untested verdicts.

papers.title: Simulation-Based Inference on EMRI Frequency Tracks: Harmonic Identification and Parameter Constraints from Search Outputs
papers.summary: Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals (EMRIs) are key targets for the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna, but their long, multi-harmonic waveforms make search and parameter estimation computationally expensive. A promising alternative is to work directly with frequency tracks recovered by a time-frequency search pipeline. We investigate whether such tracks can be used to (i) identify which harmonic(s) a recovered track corresponds to, and (ii) constrain the intrinsic EMRI parameters, including when tracks are partially masked near plunge. We first train Simulation-Based Inference (SBI) networks on large banks of azimuthal and radial fundamental-frequency tracks. For harmonic identification, we combine pairs of candidate tracks under different harmonic-label assumptions and use the resulting posterior medians and network acceptance rates to classify the correct labelling. For parameter identification, we apply a sequential (truncated-prior) SBI scheme and refine the results by cross-checking posterior samples against a time-frequency detection statistic. The correct harmonic pair is among the top-2 ranked candidates with probability $>0.99$ across masking levels, and is identified outright in 98% of cases when restricted to physically plausible candidates. Sequential SBI shrinks the intrinsic-parameter prior volume by up to $10^{13}$ within a few hours of GPU time, and the detection-statistic refinement reduces it by up to four further orders of magnitude, even for heavily masked tracks. Frequency-track-based SBI thus provides a fast, waveform-free way to identify EMRI harmonics and obtain tight prior volumes for targeted follow-up, substantially reducing the burden on subsequent MCMC-based analyses.

papers.title: Location Matters: Sparse Latent-Variance Attacks for Face Privacy against Diffusion Personalization
papers.summary: Text-to-image diffusion models can learn and reproduce an individual's identity from only a few reference photos, creating risks of unauthorized and misleading content generation. Proactive defenses address this risk by adding adversarial perturbations to facial images before release, thereby disrupting identity acquisition during downstream personalization. However, existing methods typically rely on dense $L_\infty$-bounded perturbations, whose accumulated distortions can become visible around facial structures. Recent methods improve protected-image quality, but often at the cost of reduced protection effectiveness. In this paper, we propose Sparse Encoder Attack on Latent Variance (SEAL), a sparse adversarial protection framework that modifies only 5% of the spatial locations in a facial image. SEAL combines a differentiable top-k masking scheme that jointly optimizes perturbation locations and values with a variance-oriented objective over the frozen VAE encoder's latent distribution to disrupt identity-consistent representations. A saliency-guided dispersion penalty further discourages perturbation concentration in perceptually salient facial regions. Experiments on CelebA-HQ and VGGFace2 show that SEAL achieves the best protected-image quality among the compared methods, exceeding 41 dB PSNR with 0.97 SSIM and at most 0.07 LPIPS, while reducing identity similarity to at most 0.15 after diffusion personalization. These results demonstrate that sparse location optimization enables strong identity protection while preserving high visual quality. Code and data are available at https://github.com/Lvxan/SEAL

papers.title: Semantic Chains: From Reachable Facts to Justified Answers
papers.summary: How can the facts that justify an answer be found from a question and presented as a sequence of connected statements? This paper models a context as a graph of logical facts and takes as given which expressions represent each fact. A parent fact can express a relation among its subfacts, and a preserving edge allows the content of a subfact to be recovered within a full representation of its parent. Suppose a root fact justifies the full answer and a path of preserving edges leads from that root to a fact that designates an object shared by the question and the answer. Under the conditions of the model, a search starting from the objects in the question reaches the root and covers every fact in the selected expansion. The root then admits a text that forms a single link connecting the question to the full answer and justifying it. For chains with several links, the paper gives a complete enumeration of candidate orders within the stated class and specifies when the link texts jointly preserve the justification and support every transition.

papers.title: The $χ_{c1}(3872)$ Multiplet in the Diabatic Dynamical Diquark Model
papers.summary: We apply a minimal form of the diabatic dynamical diquark model, which uses only dimeson thresholds augmented by constraints obtained from heavy-quark spin symmetry, to the hidden-charm tetraquark spectrum. We find that this model is insufficient to simultaneously reproduce the experimentally established states \(χ_{c1}(3872)\), \(T_{c\bar c1}(3900)\), and \(T_{c\bar c1}(4020)\). We therefore extend the model to its complete form, by restoring the spin- and isospin-dependent diquark-antidiquark interactions from the original adiabatic dynamical diquark model into the full diabatic potential. Aligning the resulting framework to these three states allows the remaining members of the \(Σ_g^+(1S)\) multiplet to be predicted through coupled-channel scattering simulations. The resulting resonance or bound state locations lie within approximately \(10~\mathrm{MeV}\) of the corresponding pure adiabatic mass eigenvalue predictions in all cases, indicating that the adiabatic fine-structure pattern survives the inclusion of explicit dimeson channels. We also discuss possible experimental counterparts for the unconfirmed multiplet members.

papers.title: CFAR Detection on Non-Coherently Integrated Angular Maps for mmWave Radio SLAM
papers.summary: Reliable multipath detection is essential for millimeter-wave simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM), where propagation paths reflecting off the environment provide geometric constraints beyond the dominant line-of-sight component. This paper develops constant false alarm rate (CFAR)-based detectors for beam-swept bistatic integrated sensing and communications (ISAC). Starting from conventional CFAR on the I/Q datacube, we derive a modified detector for non-coherently integrated angular power maps, where the post-integration noise statistics differ from those assumed by standard cell-averaging CFAR. To improve practicality, we introduce a multi-cell cell-under-test formulation and a plus-shaped training window that reduces computational cost while accounting for sidelobe structure. The proposed methods are evaluated on experimental 60 GHz indoor measurements using a snapshot-SLAM estimator. Compared with a singular value decomposition (SVD)-based detector, the proposed CFAR approaches reduce the overall positioning RMSE from 0.30 m to 0.24-0.26 m, with the largest improvement in non-line-of-sight snapshots. The multi-cell non-coherent detector further lowers the computational complexity without degrading positioning accuracy, demonstrating its suitability for practical multipath radio-SLAM.
papers.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication

papers.title: Information-Theoretic Threshold Design for Sparse Event Encoding in Learning Systems
papers.summary: One approach to event-driven learning is to encode continuous signals as sparse events generated when signal changes exceed a prescribed threshold. However, this threshold is typically selected empirically, with limited theoretical guidance. This paper establishes a connection between threshold-based event encoding and discretized learning systems and identifies a dimensionless ratio governing information retention. From this connection, we derive an information-sufficiency boundary using normal-condition data and formulate a data-driven criterion that selects the sparsest threshold retaining a prescribed fraction of peak discriminative information. The framework is illustrated using event cameras and evaluated on power-system fault classification. Results show that the proposed design identifies sparse operating thresholds while exposing the tradeoff between information retention, event activity, and classification performance.

papers.title: Personalized Affective Perception via Continual Learning in Human-Agent Negotiation
papers.summary: Self-interested intelligent agents that negotiate with humans should interpret nonverbal expressions and adapt their behavior accordingly. However, generic facial-affect models degrade across individuals and contexts, creating a generalization gap. We introduce an affect-adaptive negotiation strategy that incorporates Continual Learning with Imagination for Facial Expression Recognition (CLIFER) to personalize valence-arousal perception in real time. Differential feedback converts changes in valence-arousal direction and intensity into adjustments of the agent's target utility. An asynchronous architecture updates CLIFER in the background during live interaction. In a counterbalanced within-subject study in which 66 participants negotiated with a humanoid robot, the CL-enabled agent achieved significantly higher individual utility and elicited higher participant concession rates than the FaceChannel baseline. The CL condition yielded significantly higher mean arousal estimates, alongside a broader output range. Participant utility and Nash distance did not change significantly between conditions. These outcomes support the practical value of coupling continual affective personalization with differential feedback for real-time negotiation.
papers.comment: 17 pages, 11 figures. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Affective Computing

papers.title: Deep Learning for Operator Maps in Optimal Liquidation
papers.summary: We analyze the solution map of a optimal execution problem in which price dynamics are subject to a general transient impact kernel. Given the structure of the optimal trading strategy derived by Abi Jaber and Neuman in \cite{https://doi.org/10.1111/mafi.12465}, we show that the strategy is locally Lipschitz continuous with respect to the underlying model parameters governing temporary and transient price impact as well as the fundamental price process. Continuity of this map justifies the application of neural-net based approximations which take model parameters as inputs. We propose a method generating samples of the transient price impact kernel for the purposes of creating training data, and a method of projecting the kernel to a finite dimensional representation appropriate for input to a neural net, and a dimensional reduction based on the relationship between inventory and trade signal. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the trained neural net and use it to quantify the potential financial costs associated with misspecifying the transient impact kernel.

papers.title: An AI Assistant for Automating Anti-Corruption Expertise of Draft Legislation Based on the TRACE Framework
papers.summary: We present an AI assistant for automating anti-corruption expertise of draft legislation based on the TRACE architecture, designed to screen bills for corruption risks: pinpoint provisions an expert would criticise and name the regulatory defect in each. The pipeline combines a deterministic parsing core, model-guided single-provision qualification, rule-based factor assignment, and external human oversight. To evaluate the assistant, we constructed an open benchmark from the published conclusions of Ukraine's National Agency on Corruption Prevention (NAZK), comprising 132 draft laws with 474 model-extracted findings. A system flag agrees with a finding when it targets a compatible provision and an LLM judge rates the risk as the same (strict) or partly the same (lenient). On 100 draft laws, the pipeline matches 0.28 of the findings within its top ten flags using the local Gemma 4 31B model, 0.30 with Sonnet 5.5, and 0.43-0.46 across all flags (non-blind; the frozen blind baseline achieves 0.21, 95% CI 0.16-0.26). Across all runs, most misses occur on provisions that the system located but qualified as a different risk, and none of the 32 legal-collision findings was matched. On 21 acts held out from tuning, the pipeline outperforms a monolithic prompt containing the full methodology under the strict measure, though not under the lenient one, and Opus 5.5 adds nothing over Sonnet. The reported scores reflect agreement with model-extracted findings rated by an LLM judge whose two access routes agree on 73 of 74 labels, without human expert validation.

papers.title: Relativistic tidal response and mode excitation in neutron-star binaries
papers.summary: Tidal excitation links gravitational-wave emission to the internal dynamics of neutron stars. We study the dynamical tidal response of nonrotating stars with composition stratification, elastic crusts and possible first-order phase transitions. Using analytical Mano--Suzuki--Takasugi exterior solutions, we match stellar perturbations to an effective field theory and extract the poles and residues of the relativistic tidal response. Over the inspiral band, this response is accurately approximated by a sum of harmonic oscillators, as in Newtonian theory, each specified by a frequency $ω_α$ and a mode-specific tidal deformability $λ_α$, or equivalently a tidal overlap $I_α$. We couple these oscillators to relativistic effective-one-body dynamics, including gravitational redshift and frame dragging, to follow mode excitation and gravitational-wave emission. A decomposition into driven and free oscillations gives analytical mode amplitudes accurate to a few percent during inspiral. We also reconstruct the time-dependent crustal strain. In a representative $1.20+1.50\,M_\odot$ hadronic--hybrid binary, gravity, interface and shear modes produce a gravitational-wave phase shift of $\lesssim10^{-2}\,{\rm rad}$. Despite this small phase shift, gravity-mode excitation can overstrain the crust near its base, while the lowest shear mode produces widespread overstrain.

papers.title: Dyship: Leveraging Acoustic Features For Speaker Relationship Classification From Dyadic Conversations
papers.summary: We introduce DyShip, a framework for classifying speaker familiarity and kinship from dyadic conversations in the Seamless Interaction corpus. We compare five speech representations: spectrograms, MFCCs, self-supervised WavLM representations, x-vectors, and estimated articulatory movements. Spectral features perform best for familiarity classification, reaching an accuracy of 87.81%, while WavLM achieves the highest kinship accuracy of 85.17%. X-vectors and articulatory features yield weaker results on familiarity classifiaction, but shine for kinship classification, with an AUC of 0.909 for x-vectors. Most classifiers exceed previously reported human and audio language model scores on the same dataset. These findings highlight the potential of conventional acoustic features for relationship inference and motivate further investigation of the conversational cues captured by different representations.

papers.title: Beyond Accuracy: Physics-Informed Evaluation of ANN-based Power Flow Solvers under System Shift
papers.summary: Recent advances in artificial deep learning-based power flow (PF) solvers have primarily focused on improving estimation accuracy, while their physical feasibility and operational reliability under realistic system variations remain insufficiently evaluated. This paper proposes a physics-informed evaluation framework for deep learning-based PF solvers under topology and load distribution shifts. Beyond conventional voltage-domain errors, the framework incorporates KCL gaps, branch-flow gaps, KVL residuals, continuous feasibility scores, and strict, practical, and relaxed PF feasibility rates. Four case studies are designed to investigate topology shifts, mixed topology training, load distribution shifts, and combined topology distribution shifts. Eight ANN architectures, including graph input models, load-only baselines, and physics-informed neural networks, are evaluated under consistent settings. The results demonstrate that low estimation errors do not necessarily correspond to physically feasible or operationally reliable PF solutions, particularly under combined system shifts. The proposed framework establishes an initial foundation and analysis for the development and verification of trustworthy deep learning-based PF solvers, providing support for their reliable deployment in future AI-enabled power system analysis.

papers.title: Unveiling the Extreme Universe with Recent IACT Discoveries
papers.summary: Very-high-energy (VHE, $E \gtrsim 50$\,GeV) $γ$-ray astronomy has evolved into an indispensable pillar of modern astroparticle physics, offering a direct view of non-thermal particle acceleration, cosmic-ray origins, and fundamental physics. Ground-based Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes (IACTs) have driven this revolution over the past two decades. In this plenary review, presented at the 9th Heidelberg International Symposium on High-Energy Gamma-Ray Astronomy (Gamma 2026), I provide a synthesis of recent breakthrough physics discoveries achieved by current IACT arrays (H.E.S.S., MAGIC, and VERITAS) alongside early scientific achievements from the Large-Sized Telescope prototype (LST-1) of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO). Key highlights include the definitive establishment of recurrent novae as transient cosmic-ray proton accelerators via RS Ophiuchi; spatially resolved multi-TeV emission from the relativistic jet termination shocks of microquasars; the discovery of a 20 TeV pulsed radiation component from the Vela pulsar, challenging established magnetospheric emission paradigms; precision measurements of the Galactic Center diffuse ridge spectrum favoring a high-energy cutoff; the detection of distant flat-spectrum radio quasars at $z \sim 1$ (OP 313 and PKS 0346-27), providing tight cosmological constraints on the Extragalactic Background Light; multi-wavelength afterglow detections of $γ$-ray bursts including GRB 221009A; and world-leading joint indirect dark matter limits from dwarf spheroidal galaxy and Galactic Center halo analyses. Together with algorithmic advances in deep learning reconstruction and the ongoing construction of CTAO, these milestones demonstrate the enduring vitality and future trajectory of ground-based $γ$-ray astrophysics.

papers.title: StaRSE: Compact Russian Sentence Embeddings with a Sign-Coded Static Encoder
papers.summary: Transformer sentence encoders provide strong retrieval quality, but their inference cost becomes a bottleneck when embeddings must be produced on CPUs or refreshed frequently. We introduce StaRSE, a compact Russian static sentence encoder that removes Transformer inference at deployment time: token directions are stored as sign bits, token norms are stored separately, and sentences are encoded by mean pooling over norm-scaled sign directions. StaRSE is initialized from ruBERT-base, fine-tuned on Russian adjacent-sentence and task-shaped pairs, and post-trained with a contrastive stage that directly optimizes the sign-projected token table. On RuMTEB, StaRSE reaches a task mean of $51.16$, $7.98$ points above the strongest included static baseline. The packaged model occupies $11.3$ MiB and has a mean CPU latency of $0.08$ ms per sentence, compared with an estimated $55.7$ MiB 16-bit parameter footprint and $1.43$ ms mean CPU latency for the closest-quality contextual encoder. Ablations examine adjacent-sentence supervision, token norms, and direct sign-projected post-training.

papers.title: Banding instabilities in poroelastic media under flow-driven compaction
papers.summary: When cross-linked poroelastic media are subjected to a hydrostatic pressure difference, they compact, remaining fully swollen on their uppermost surface and becoming increasingly compressed with depth. A critical unexplored effect of cross-linking and resistance to shear deformation is investigated, which is not seen in classical models of poroelastic media treated as free elastic spheres, and resists the kind of compressive compaction that characterises these systems. Eventually, a steady-state profile dependent on osmotic, shear and transport properties is reached, supporting a uniform interstitial flow wherein the medium acts like a passive filter. In this paper, we show how these steady-state profiles are not necessarily stable, and propose a mechanism for the formation of instabilities, wherein some regions of the medium swell and others compact, forming distinctive horizontal or vertical banding patterns. In the latter case, these bands appear qualitatively to be higher-permeability conduits or channels, similar to wormholes or tunnels seen in granular media. It is possible to quantify the effect of changing the pressure head on the growth rate of instabilities and the separation lengthscale in this channelisation case, and how material properties like shear stiffness and dependence of permeability on porosity affect the dynamics of instability. Critically, it is shown that these instabilities are a fluid-mechanical effect, with an entirely new mechanism based on the porosity--permeability relationship and not on elastic effects. With an understanding of these mechanisms, we can derive insight into channelisation in poroelastic systems in geophysics, human biology and industry.
papers.comment: Submitted to the Journal of Fluid Mechanics

papers.title: Probing for anisotropies at different angular scales in the arrival directions of the cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory
papers.summary: Studies of the arrival-direction distribution of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays are crucial for revealing their origin. In this work, we investigate the distribution of the arrival directions of events detected with the Pierre Auger Observatory over different angular scales. To do this, we adopt a novel method where we use a von Mises--Fisher distribution to model the excesses with respect to isotropic expectations. This method allows us to study the distribution of arrival directions over different angular scales consistently and simultaneously. We consider the events in different energy bins above 4 EeV detected from 1$^\text{st}$ January 2004 to 31$^\text{st}$ December 2022, i.e. during the entire Phase~I of the Pierre Auger Observatory, with a total exposure of $123{,}000$ km$^2$ sr yr. The most significant excess in the bins considered is a dipolar modulation in the energy range (8--16) EeV, which is compatible with previous findings of the Pierre Auger Collaboration. A dipolar modulation appears to be present for the higher energies considered as well, and at the highest energies, i.e. above 32 EeV, we find indications of its coexistence with an overdensity of intermediate angular scale, located in the Centaurus region.
authors: J. R. T. de Mello Neto

papers.title: Intelligent Carbon Emission-aware Radio Unit Activation Control in Dense Heterogeneous Energy 6G Networks
papers.summary: Base stations account for a dominant share of energy consumption and operational carbon emissions in radio access networks. In O-RAN deployments with heterogeneous energy sources, however, minimizing energy consumption alone does not necessarily minimize carbon emissions. In this work, we investigate carbon-aware DRL for RU sleep control. Under the adopted source-matched operational accounting model, renewable-matched RUs are assigned zero direct operational emissions, whereas non-renewable-supplied RUs incur operational emissions. The problem is formulated as a Markov decision process and evaluated using two carbon-aware reward formulations and a conventional energy--QoS reward baseline. We implement and compare TD3, PPO, and a heuristic method under realistic mobility and 3GPP channel models across multiple renewable-matched RU layouts and traffic loads. Simulation results show that TD3 learns more energy-efficient activation policies than PPO, achieving approximately 3%--6% lower energy consumption in representative scenarios. TD3 also achieves 8%--12% lower operational emissions than PPO in scenarios with a low proportion of renewable-matched RUs and up to a 20% reduction relative to the heuristic baseline under moderate renewable availability and high traffic load. Moreover, the joint energy,carbon and QoS reward achieves approximately 12%--28% lower operational emissions than the energy and QoS reward, while maintaining comparable energy consumption.

papers.title: From Growth to Devices: Oxygen-Controlled Superconductivity in BSCCO Thin Films
papers.summary: Realizing device-compatible high-$T_c$ superconductors requires simultaneous control of oxygen stoichiometry and tolerance to nanofabrication. Here, we investigate sputtered Bi$_2$Sr$_2$Ca$_{n-1}$Cu$_n$O$_{2n+4+δ}$ (BSCCO) thin films and establish a direct link between annealing conditions, oxygen incorporation, and superconducting transport. By independently varying the annealing temperature and duration, we identify an optimal annealing condition of $860\,^{\circ}$C for 3\,h, which yields the highest superconducting transition temperature and the narrowest transition among the investigated samples. X-ray diffraction, electron microscopy, and X-ray photoemission spectroscopy reveal a non-monotonic evolution of lattice oxygen, which governs hole doping in the CuO$_2$ planes and produces the characteristic dome-like dependence of $T_c$ on doping concentration. We further translate these optimized films into micro-devices to assess fabrication-induced effects, via micro-bridges as well as a planar Josephson junction. We demonstrate devices fabricated via both lift-off and focused ion beam (FIB) patterning methods -- proving the fabrication compatibility of these films. Importantly, we demonstrate their air-stability for extended periods of time (2 months). The combined insights offer practical guidelines for integrating cuprate thin films into superconducting electronics and quantum device architectures.

papers.title: The Multiscale Principle in phase transition: Geometric structure, thermodynamic entropy, and dynamical instability
papers.summary: Scaling and multi-scaling are two guiding principles for understanding nature or even commerce and industrial outcome. In the realm of critical phenomena, scaling laws describe the behavior of physical quantities near a continuous phase transition. This is a complex phenomena where systems exhibit critical fluctuations and long-range correlations, challenging classical formulations such as the fluctuation-dissipation theorem (FDT). In particular, near critical points, the divergence of the correlation length and the emergence of fractal geometry in spin clusters suggest the need for alternative frameworks. In this work, we explore the connection between critical exponents, fractal dimensions, and the thermodynamic formalism known as the Principium Luxuriae. By linking the thermodynamic fractal dimension D to the correlation length and entropy variations, we reinterpret energy dissipation in terms of multiscale processes. This approach allows us to reproduce effective scaling tendencies associated with the critical behavior of the 2d Ising model and provides new insight into how systems redistribute energy macroscopically during phase transitions. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the decrease in D near the critical temperature marks a transition toward macroscopic coherence, where the system begins to dissipate energy across its entire scale. This unified behavior, however, induces a heightened sensitivity to perturbations, where local fluctuations are transmitted globally through the fractal network. This mechanism establishes a direct bridge between geometric structure, thermodynamic entropy, and the onset of dynamical instability (chaos) as the system approaches criticality.

papers.title: The PAU Survey: Dissecting strong-lensing systems with narrow-band photometric redshifts
papers.summary: Wide-field imaging surveys such as Euclid will identify large samples of strong-lens candidates, whose scientific use requires redshifts for both deflectors and lensed sources. Source redshifts are challenging because faint arcs are blended with foreground light. We test lens-model-informed photometry on eight known strong lenses, using broad-band models to define component regions, point-reflection subtraction to reduce contamination, and PAU Survey narrow bands combined with five HSC or CFHT broad bands. BCNz estimates separate lens and source redshift distributions without imposing their expected ordering. All eight lens redshift peaks agree with spectroscopy within $|δ_z|\leq0.014$, where $δ_z=(z_b-z_{\rm spec})/(1+z_{\rm spec})$. Four source peaks, all at $z_{\rm s}^{\rm spec}\leq1.23$, agree within $|δ_z|\leq0.025$. Symmetric subtraction reduces the median source $|δ_z|$ from 0.336 to 0.071. At $|δ_z|<0.05$, narrow- plus broad-band photometry yields eight lens and four source matches, versus three and two using EAZY with broad bands alone. These results demonstrate component redshift recovery in blended systems and support redshift-based lens-candidate assessment alongside morphology and colour. Larger narrow-band surveys, including J-PAS, could extend this approach, pending uncertainty calibration and blind candidate tests.

papers.title: Model-Based Authoring of SOC Simulation Exercises for Cybersecurity Education
papers.summary: Cybersecurity training and classroom exercises with a virtual Security Operations Center (SOC) combine alerts, evidence, timeline entries, learner tasks, and assessment items that must remain consistent across an evolving incident. This paper presents a model-based authoring method in which a technical and educational specification is used to construct an incident exercise model and a large language model (LLM) generates selected scenario text based on that model. The incident exercise model combines an incident model of events, objects, and evidence with an exercise orchestration model of SOC alerts, timeline entries, learner tasks, and assessment items. The method is implemented in a Virtual SOC prototype and evaluated using a phishing-to-ransomware reference exercise. Its incident exercise model contains eight incident events, eight incident objects, six evidence items, seven alerts in five batches, 13 timeline entries including 12 learner tasks, and five representative assessment items. GLM-5.3-generated alert descriptions are inserted and a separate validator checks references, ordering, evidence links, assessment completeness, and selected fixed fields. Validation is demonstrated with reference data, resulting in true-negative outcomes for valid data and true-positive outcomes for deliberately placed inconsistencies. The resulting exercise package is executable within the Virtual SOC learner environment. Overall, the evaluation indicates consistency across the involved model elements and establishes the feasibility of the model-based and generative approach.
papers.comment: Presented at 2026 6th Asia Education Technology Symposium (AETS 2026), November 2026. Accepted for publication in the conference proceedings. Official publication forthcoming

papers.title: Dual-Parabola Interpolator: A Low-Bias Peak Estimator for Distributed Radar Synchronization
papers.summary: Coherent distributed radar processing requires accurate wireless synchronization.
