papers.summary: What if a single face-facing camera could sense your surroundings---through your eyes? We introduce EyeQ, which explores corneal reflection as a modality for context-aware mobile interaction. Traditional vision-based context sensing relies on world-facing cameras that demand explicit aiming or dual-camera setups; EyeQ instead shows that an off-the-shelf VLM can read scene context from corneal reflections captured with a smartphone camera. To recover usable detail from mobile corneal crops, EyeQ pairs on-device iris-guided capture with server-side AI enhancement, then leverages VLMs to extract scene types, names, and objects from warped, unfamiliar eye-image sequences. In an N=10 study, we characterize how capture conditions shape reflection fidelity, evaluate what VLMs detect, misclassify, and hallucinate, and demonstrate interaction opportunities, including detecting a steering wheel to distinguish drivers from passengers. This work reframes the eye in HCI---from a target for gaze estimation to a passive mirror of one's surroundings---and examines the privacy tensions it raises.

papers.title: Human and Machine Annotations Predict Brain Responses to Naturalistic Movies Across Development
papers.summary: Naturalistic movie watching provides a powerful framework for studying dynamic brain function, but linking movie content to neural responses typically relies on labor-intensive human annotation. We investigated whether multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can provide scalable socio-affective and semantic annotations for naturalistic fMRI. We compared MLLM-generated theory-of-mind (ToM) and valence ratings with human ratings and with regional BOLD responses across three animated movies. For two of these movies, we combined machine-derived visual features, natural-language scene descriptions, and socio-affective ratings in an ROI-wise encoding model of fMRI data from 66 participants aged 5--22 years. MLLM ratings partially tracked human judgments, but their neural correspondence differed by construct and model: ToM showed the most consistent human--machine overlap in visual cortex, whereas valence correspondence was largely movie dependent. In the encoding model, visual features yielded the strongest and most widespread prediction, whereas scene descriptions were more spatially selective, concentrated in dorsal-attention and visual regions and extending into right lateral temporal cortex. Age-group comparisons suggested feature-specific developmental differences: scene-description encoding in dorsal-attention cortex was higher in the oldest group, whereas visual-feature encoding in salience/ventral-attention, limbic, and control networks peaked in the middle group. Together, these findings indicate that MLLM-generated annotations capture meaningful aspects of human judgments and neural responses, supporting MLLMs as a scalable complement to, rather than a replacement for, human annotation in naturalistic neuroimaging.

papers.title: Herding with Multiple States: When the Prior Matters
papers.summary: In sequential observational learning with more than two states, the same information structure and preferences can yield learning for some full-support priors and herding for others. This disproves a conjecture of Kartik, Lee, Liu, and Rappoport (2024, working-paper version). In the counterexample, the cascade region has nonempty interior, yet learning occurs for generic full-support priors outside it. Focusing on information and preferences, we introduce two necessary conditions for learning. Escapability requires that signals can provide arbitrarily strong evidence that any given action is ex post suboptimal; pairwise escapability is its pairwise variant. If escapability fails, herding occurs for some initial prior; if pairwise escapability fails, it occurs for every full-support prior. For a class of environments with interval optimality and monotone likelihood ratios, escapability completely characterizes learning and herding independently of the full-support initial prior. With location-shift signals, this characterization reduces to pairwise distinguishability, a generalization of unbounded beliefs (Smith and Sørensen, 2000).

papers.title: Multifidelity Operator Inference for Non-intrusive Model Reduction under Data Scarcity
papers.summary: Many-query analyses, in which a computational model is repeatedly evaluated, play an important role in uncertainty quantification and optimization for engineering design. However, many-query analyses can be prohibitively expensive when considering high-fidelity numerical models, especially those governed by partial differential equations (PDEs). Surrogate modeling replaces costly simulations with cheap approximations, enabling practical uncertainty quantification and design workflows. Machine learning (ML) approaches to surrogate modeling have gained significant traction in the development of surrogate models due to their non-intrusive nature; they do not require access to the underlying simulation code. The Operator Inference (OpInf) approach, in particular, fits reduced operators to state and corresponding time derivative data. However, high-fidelity training data is scarce due to limited computational budgets, and OpInf models trained on such scarce data often exhibit high variance, a critical liability in high-risk engineering design. We propose Multifidelity Operator Inference (MF-OpInf), which reduces this variance by supplementing scarce high-fidelity snapshots with abundant low-fidelity data drawn from coarser discretizations of the same problem. MF-OpInf handles data across varying fidelity levels by utilizing a multifidelity linear regression framework to estimate the reduced operators. Numerical experiments on model PDE problems demonstrate that MF-OpInf predicts PDE solution fields with higher accuracy compared to the high-fidelity-only OpInf with the same computational budget.

papers.title: Optimal Trading Speed on Blockchain
papers.summary: On blockchain-based exchanges, faster blocks weaken the priority-fee competition among arbitrageurs and shift rents from the block producer to them. Equilibrium liquidity peaks at an interior block speed; beyond a threshold, an active liquidity provider cream-skims and passive capital shrinks. Evidence from the Base Flashblocks upgrade, a tenfold block-speed increase, confirms the predictions. Priority-fee bids decrease sharply and arbitrageurs' net profit rises. The active liquidity provider rebalances faster, avoids toxic flow, and earns a higher profit. Pool depth falls and effective spreads widen despite closer tracking of external prices.

papers.title: Nuclear medium and final state interaction effects in $η$ production induced by $ν_μ(\barν_μ)$ at SBN and DUNE energies
papers.summary: We investigate nuclear-medium modification and final-state interaction in charged- and neutral-current $ν_μ(\barν_μ)$-induced $η$-meson production on $^{12}\mathrm{C}$ and $^{40}\mathrm{Ar}$. The nuclear medium is described within a local density approximation, incorporating in-medium modifications of the $N^*(1535)$ resonance, which is known to play the dominant role in $η$ production through its $N η$ decay channel. The subsequent propagation and absorption of the $η$ meson in the nucleus are simulated using a Monte Carlo approach. We find that nuclear-medium modifications and final state interaction lead to substantial suppression of the production cross section, highlighting the importance of nuclear effects in interpreting $η$ production data. Our results provide valuable theoretical input for the analysis of $η$-production at the ongoing SBND and MicroBooNE experiments and the forthcoming DUNE experiment.

papers.title: Fractional-Order Hybrid SIR Forecasting of COVID-19 in Bangladesh and the United States: Memory Effects and Out-of-Sample Evaluation
papers.summary: Fractional-order epidemic models are often justified by memory, yet whether memory improves forecasts is rarely tested out of sample. We extend a hybrid SIR framework, in which a daily transmission rate is reconstructed from reported cases and then forecast, to Caputo fractional order $α\in(0,1]$. We prove well-posedness, conservation, positivity and a linearized threshold at disease-free states, and derive a Grünwald-Letnikov reconstruction that reduces exactly to the integer-order one at $α=1$. Our main theoretical result shows that for $α<1$ the influence of the unknown initial infectious count vanishes, but no faster than $t^{-α}$; after 332 daily steps it is about $4.4\times10^{8}$ times larger at $α=0.9$ than at $α=1$. In out-of-sample forecasting over 27 weekly origins, the effect of memory depends on the setting. In Bangladesh the integer order gives the lowest error for linear and constant-rate forecasts in 47 of 48 settings. In the United States, where reported cases reached about 18% of the population, a fractional order lowers the linear forecaster's error in all 12 comparisons in 2021 but raises the constant-rate forecaster's, with no difference significant after Holm adjustment. Against standard baselines, the SIR-based linear forecaster was more accurate than the classical SIR model and a neural network without SIR structure, and competitive with ARIMA: in the United States the fractional linear forecaster had the lowest error of all methods (seven-day MAPE 7.54% against 9.14% for ARIMA), whereas in Bangladesh ARIMA had the lowest MAPE, with no significant difference from ARIMA in either country. The choice of a fractional order should rest on out-of-sample evidence rather than in-sample fit.
papers.comment: 23 pages, 5 figures, 9 tables. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24057230

papers.title: Lightweight Deep Learning Framework for Astrocyte-Centric 3D Reconstruction across Normal and Stress-associated Ultrastructural States
papers.summary: The morphology of astrocytes is closely associated with their ability to support and modulate neural circuit functions; however, its reconstruction from volume electron microscopy (vEM) data remains labor-intensive and computationally resource-intensive, placing substantial barriers on its broader adoption and scalability despite the high spatial resolution of vEM. We present AstroSeg-vEM, a lightweight, astrocyte-centric framework for morphology-preserving astrocyte segmentation, 3D reconstruction, and quantitative morphological analysis in vEM images. AstroSeg-vEM combines transformer-based 2D segmentation with dedicated post-processing methods and operates directly on high-resolution EM sections, making it well suited to anisotropic vEM data and downstream proofreading workflows while preserving the full in-plane resolution of the original EM data. Across four mouse hippocampal datasets representing normal and morphologically defined stress-associated astrocyte ultrastructural states, AstroSeg-vEM demonstrates robust performance and generalization, achieving average Dice and weighted Dice values of 0.92 and 0.95, respectively, on a held-out test dataset. Its lightweight architecture enables efficient, high-fidelity reconstruction on consumer-grade hardware, providing a scalable and accessible platform for large-scale astrocyte ultrastructure analysis and future astrocyte-neuron interaction studies.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in npj Imaging. 19 pages, 4 figures, 6 tables, including Supplementary Material. Code is available at https://github.com/QuIN-Lab/AstroSeg-vEM

papers.title: POEM: Output-Relative Block-Sparse Attention for Long-Context Prefilling
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong capabilities across diverse applications, making both safety and utility essential for reliable deployment. Jailbreak attacks use diverse forms of adversarial prompting to bypass alignment safeguards and induce LLMs to generate harmful responses. Some representation-based defenses regulate internal activations using predefined steering directions or learned safety regions. However, adapting intervention to each input without a predefined representational target while limiting over-refusal remains a challenge. In this paper, we propose Target-free Entropy-guided Residual Modulation (TERM), an inference-time defense that uses prompt-calibrated attention entropy deviations to guide adaptive modulation of the model's own residual updates. Attention patterns vary across prompts and decoding steps, making raw entropy values difficult to interpret as a consistent signal for intervention. We therefore calibrate attention entropy against each prompt's own prefill baseline to establish an input-specific reference for reducing unnecessary intervention on benign requests. Adaptive scale normalization and temporal accumulation then account for differences in deviation scale and persistence to determine intervention strength. The resulting signal controls bounded scaling of the model's own residual updates, without relying on a predefined safety direction. We compare our method with seven defenses on seven jailbreak attacks and two over-refusal benchmarks across Llama, Qwen, and Gemma models, including Qwen3 models from 0.6B to 32B. Results show our method improves jailbreak robustness while maintaining low over-refusal on benign safety-sensitive requests with modest inference overhead.

Results show our method improves jailbreak robustness while maintaining low over-refusal on benign safety-sensitive requests with modest inference overhead.

papers.title: Quasinormal overtones and grey-body factors of Frolov black holes
papers.summary: We investigate scalar quasinormal modes (QNMs), with particular attention to overtones, and grey-body factors of Frolov black holes, which interpolate between the Reissner--Nordström (RN) and Hayward limits. Over the allowed ranges of charge $q$ and regularization parameter $α_0$, all QNM frequencies have negative imaginary parts, confirming stability against scalar perturbations. Increasing either $q$ or $α_0$ can trigger overtone outbursts, with the Frolov threshold shifted to smaller parameter values than in the RN or Hayward cases. Angular momentum does not eliminate the outburst but postpones its onset from $n=1$ at $l=0$ to $n\geq 2$ at $l=1$. Comparisons of the effective potential show that, for $l=1$, charge raises the barrier peak much more strongly than $α_0$, while the clearest deviations from the Hayward and RN references are localized near the horizon. Using the QNM--grey-body correspondence at $l=1$, we find that overtone corrections are essential, and the amended formula substantially outperforms the eikonal truncation. At fixed frequency, both $q$ and $α_0$ suppress transmission, with charge being the dominant factor, consistent with the stronger barrier enhancement under the charge scan.

papers.title: Navigating relational agency in AI feedback musicianship: a diffractive dialogue
papers.summary: Musical AI systems behave in non-linear, dynamic ways that exceed the tool-oriented framings inherited from earlier instrument design. Existing frames of control and ensemble interaction do not articulate the entangled, relational agency that emerges when performers work with AI feedback instruments over time. We examine a duet practice with two AI-enabled feedback instruments, Sù and Agentier, in which feedback operates at the inner level of the AI's recurrent processes and the outer loop of musical interaction between performer, instrument, and co-performer. Our work draws on agential realism and a diffractive dialogue methodology to read our independent reflections through one another across five performances, examining how agency is enacted between performers and AI instruments. We find that control and agency are relational and shift across performances; musical textures enact feedback moments of control with performers; reaching a productive feedback environment is itself a shared exploratory act; and performers maintain their instruments through funnelling and injection, developing the skill of navigating agency along a continuous spectrum. Feedback musicianship with AI instruments demands navigation of this relational agency, displacing the leading-versus-responding binary that initially framed our reflections. This work contributes a materially-grounded vocabulary for AI feedback musicianship and a model of human-AI creative collaboration in which mutual agency is worked for through practice rather than designed in.

papers.title: Ayurvedic Rasayana Restores Lipid Homeostasis in Liver: Insights from Systems Biology Studies
papers.summary: MASLD and obesity characterized by hepatic lipid accumulation are known risk factors to manifest into Type 2 diabetes (T2D). Increased hepatic lipids due to interorgan cross talk leads de novo lipid synthesis which induce insulin resistance in multiple organs resulting in hyperglycemia. We evaluated two known lipid reducing Ayurvedic formulations, Arogyavardhini Rasa (AVR) and Nishamalaki Rasayana (NA), to understand their mechanistic basis. Network medicine-based analyses identified 128 phytochemicals in AVR and 182 in NA that met the predefined filtering criteria. The reported targets of both formulations showed significant network proximity to genes associated with T2D, fatty liver disease and obesity. An integrated knowledge graph linking formulations, phytochemicals, protein targets, FDA-approved drugs and disease genes enabling systems-level exploration of these relationships revealed eight targets, namely PPARA, PPARG, AKT1, SIRT1, TNF, PPARD, SERPINE1, and ACE which were common to both drugs. In the animal study, both formulations reduced high-fat-diet-associated increases in blood glucose, cholesterol, liver enzymes, macrovesicular and microvesicular hepatic steatosis. Untargeted liver metabolomics showed AVR and NA treatment restored sugar and nucleotide, pentose phosphate, bile and lipid metabolism pathways that were perturbed in response to high fat diet. Taken together, AVR and NA restored hepatic lipid homeostasis and inhibited manifestation of T2D.

papers.title: Tabular Foundation Models in Financial Predictions
papers.summary: This technical note introduces tabular foundation models (TFMs) to accounting research and evaluates their performance in one common benchmark task: predicting firms' next-year earnings changes. TFMs produce numeric predictions and learn in context, without post-release training or tuning, making them natural and easy to use for forecasting. The TFMs we study are pretrained on synthetic tabular data, so they avoid look-ahead bias from memorizing firms' outcomes. We compare Google Research's TabFM with a fine-tuned open-weight large language model developed in recent accounting research and with several tree-based models. TabFM is more accurate than all comparison models. It is also faster and less computationally intensive than the large language model. Several tree-based specifications produce predictions more quickly than TabFM, so choosing between them involves a trade-off between accuracy and speed. We conclude that TFMs have promise as a new tool for forecasting in accounting and finance. However, our evaluation is based on a single benchmark task, and no class of models is likely to dominate in all settings.

papers.title: Perspicacious: An Educational Intelligence Platform for Instructional Designers
papers.summary: Designing effective instruction requires instructional designers to create assessment questions aligned with clearly defined knowledge components (KCs). These KCs represent specific knowledge or skills that students must acquire. This process is often time-consuming and relies heavily on expert labor. Although AI for education research has produced a growing body of automated question-generation and KC-discovery methods, few have moved beyond research prototypes into user-friendly tools that instructional designers can readily use. To bridge the research-to-practice gap, we developed and evaluated an educational intelligence platform that unifies question generation and KC discovery behind a single interface to support instructional content development. Named "Perspicacious," our platform aims to help instructional designers "see through" complex data and algorithms to derive instructional insights. A cost model calibrated on 17 production runs revealed a cost-time trade-off: extracting KCs from a 576-question bank cost US $1.98-4.11 and took 36-158 minutes to complete, depending on the budget. A formative, partially Wizard-of-Oz study with eight instructional designers found strong perceived usability (mean SUS 78.8) and surfaced concrete requirements that we treat as prerequisites for deployment.

papers.title: Repertoires of Contention: Building computational tools and infrastructures for community resistance to bitcoin mining
papers.summary: Recent work in human-computer interaction and allied fields has sought to engage community members as co-designers, facilitators, and decision makers to challenge structural power barriers and knowledge gaps. In this paper, we apply a diverse set of computational techniques to engage and address community concerns surrounding the socio-environmental impacts of the Greenidge Bitcoin mining power plant facility in upstate New York. Through collaborative interactions with community groups, addressing problems ranging from regulatory inertia to thermal water pollution, we aim to facilitate not just the production of new and critical environmental knowledge but also new computationally-supported repertoires of contention: means of contesting the unequal relations of knowledge and power that structure and often determine the outcomes of environmental controversies. We argue such engagements can help support more politically engaged forms of HCI, oriented towards efforts to redress and repair disparities in wealth, knowledge, and influence through strategic sociotechnical interventions and alliances.

papers.title: EJAI: Judgment-Preserving Civic AI for Data Center Environmental Justice
papers.summary: Communities in the United States and around the world are contesting data centers, the physical infrastructure of AI. These disputes pose environmental justice issues: residents must weigh unevenly distributed burdens using evidence scattered across metrics, corporate claims, policy documents, and public testimony. A formative study with 10 users showed that dashboards and single-agent AI can settle questions before people examine that evidence. Here we present EJAI, a source-grounded system that links an interactive map, retrieved evidence, missing-data statements, and two stakeholder personas that allow people to inspect evidence and form their own policy recommendations. In a small functional benchmark of 21 queries, retrieved evidence supported 98.4% of factual claims and the system acknowledged missing evidence in 32 of 33 cases. Persona alignment carried a grounding cost: the Corporate Executive omitted some evidence that conflicted with its assigned priorities. In a within-subjects study, 15 participants acting as residents prepared for a simulated town hall. Some checked cited AI claims while treating map metrics as official, some made conditional recommendations with safeguards such as water-use disclosure, and some found the personas simplified or biased. Our results suggest that civic AI can support preparation for public reasoning when it makes evidence, gaps, and disagreement open to inspection, and that corpus imbalance and two-sided personas remain open justice concerns.

papers.title: Pseudo-marginal Sampling for Selective Inference
papers.summary: Inference after adaptive selection must account for selection bias. One approach is to condition on the selected event, but for complex selection procedures, the resulting conditional distribution can be analytically intractable and require sampling-based methods. Rejection sampling provides a natural baseline: it repeatedly draws from a proposal and retains only samples that reproduce the observed selection. This can be prohibitively expensive when the selection event is rare. We address this computational bottleneck with a pseudo-marginal Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm that samples from the selective distribution. Using a weak Poincaré inequality, we analyze its computational efficiency relative to rejection sampling and identify when it can offer substantial gains. In the classical file-drawer problem, we derive precise computational costs for both methods, illustrating exponential improvement as the selection event becomes increasingly rare. In numerical experiments involving complex selection procedures without tractable conditional distributions, the pseudo-marginal sampler is often hundreds of times more efficient than rejection sampling, while the resulting tests achieve nominal selective Type I error.

papers.title: Data-Efficient Unlearning-Based Backdoor Detection in Federated Learning
papers.summary: Detecting backdoor attacks in federated learning (FL) is challenging because malicious clients can manipulate the global model while preserving main-task performance. Static model-update statistics may therefore fail to clearly distinguish malicious from benign clients. Unlearning-based detectors instead probe client models through loss ascent on clean server data, but detection performance degrades with scarce proxy data. We propose Screening via Unlearning Response Analysis (SURA), a data-efficient detector. SURA reuses the same small clean proxy across multiple train-mode loss-ascent steps, strengthening client responses without additional clean data. For federated vision models with batch normalization (BN), repeated probing also changes BN running statistics and can confound endpoint measurements. SURA addresses this by restoring the shared pre-probe BN state only at readout while preserving the parameter changes induced by probing. This separates repeated probing from response measurement and removes BN drift and the interaction between parameter and BN-state changes from the readout. Across six backdoor attacks, SURA uses only 10 clean server images, outperforms methods under the same data budget, and approaches the robustness obtained with much larger proxy sets.

papers.title: Differentially Private Statistical Inference for Rankings from Pairwise Comparisons
papers.summary: Reliable inference for rankings of large language models based on human pairwise comparisons must preserve the privacy of individual preference records. To meet this need, we develop methods for score and rank inference under the Bradley-Terry model with edge differential privacy. For an objective-perturbed estimator, a new leave-one-out analysis establishes finite-sample bounds on Euclidean and entrywise estimation errors. For sufficiently dense comparison graphs, the error bounds extend to smaller privacy budgets, including regimes in which its privacy term dominates its statistical term. A uniform asymptotic expansion yields asymptotically valid confidence intervals for individual scores and pairwise score differences. To improve finite-sample performance, we account for both regularization bias and privacy-induced randomness by combining a plug-in ridge-bias correction with Gaussian-Laplace calibration. We further establish a bootstrap procedure for simultaneous rank inference, providing asymptotically valid confidence sets for individual ranks and tests of top-$K$ membership. When the comparison probability is public and known, all proposed inferential procedures require no additional privacy budget. We evaluate finite-sample performance through simulations and apply the proposed methods to rank large language models for creative writing.

papers.title: Leveraging Psychophysical Attentional Distribution for Gaze-Augmented Reward Modeling
papers.summary: Integrating human feedback into language models has gained increasing attention as a means to align model outputs with human preferences, with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) serving as a prominent framework for preference-based alignment. Recent studies have incorporated eye-tracking (ET) data as an additional supervisory signal for reward model training, grounding reward learning in human reading behavior. Building on this approach, we extend prior fixation-centric models by leveraging established findings from cognitive psychology on human letter recognition. Specifically, we model visual attention as a spatially graded distribution centered on the current gaze location and incorporate this representation into reward model training. Our results show that the reward model trained with the proposed gaze distribution achieves higher preference prediction accuracy than a baseline model. Moreover, some results from our experiments are qualitatively consistent with established findings on human attention during reading, suggesting that they potentially capture cognitively meaningful aspects of human attention allocation.
papers.comment: 15 pages, 4 figures. Accepted to the 40th Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026 Main Track)

papers.title: Obvious Group Manipulations and Top Trading Cycles
papers.summary: We introduce a group version of non-obvious manipulability, which is stronger than the original definition by Troyan and Morrill (2020) and weaker than group strategy-proofness, and study its implications in Shapley-Scarf housing markets. We provide several characterizations of the Top Trading Cycles mechanism using the new condition.

papers.title: A Hierarchical View of Ecological Encounters
papers.summary: Encounters between individuals, or between individuals and entities like vehicles, are central to understanding a host of topics in ecology and related fields. Problems of mate-finding, predator-prey interactions, pathogen spread, and animal interactions with infrastructure all hinge on encounters. Historically, however, encounters have been difficult to observe at scale, and the relevant theoretical frameworks---which ultimately derive from the ideal gas law---have been badly mismatched to the underlying biology. Here, we synthesize and provide ecological context for recent developments in mathematics, statistics, and physics that permit the inclusion of more biological realism into encounter-related models. We propose an encounters--interactions--outcomes hierarchical framework for organizing core concepts across a diverse range of ecological scenarios. Implemented as a hierarchical Bayesian model, our framework permits tight connections with multi-level ecological data relevant to the estimation of encounter rates and their downstream impacts on interactions and outcomes. Throughout, we emphasize how the ongoing revolution in animal biologging yields empirical datasets that can be employed to quantify otherwise inaccessible rate parameters and their dependencies. We conclude with a series of major open questions about encounters designed to spur conceptual and quantitative integration across models, data sources, and ecological levels of organization.

papers.title: AdaFCP: Local Neural Functional Representations for Industrial Change Detection
papers.summary: Industrial sensor measurements often form ordered functional profiles in which persistent operating-regime changes may be confined to short within-cycle regions. Fixed projections can dilute such changes, whereas data-adaptive representation learning complicates reliable statistical testing. This paper proposes adaptive functional change-point detection (AdaFCP) for retrospective detection of a single functional mean change. A compact window and neural basis learn a change-sensitive functional projection by matching the CUSUM path of projected scores to single-change templates. Standardized peak-CUSUM scanning then provides the detection statistic and transition estimate, while the fitted weights identify the contributing within-cycle region. Theoretical analysis characterizes the population path-matching signal and derives an optimal-direction signal-to-noise benchmark. Full-pipeline permutation calibration accounts for adaptive representation learning and restart selection, providing finite-sample false-positive control under exchangeability. A decision-preserving early-stopping variant, AdaFCP-ES, further reduces calibration effort without altering the fixed-budget test decision. Simulations demonstrate advantages over several fixed representations for localized oscillatory changes, while strong analytic and multiscale controls remain competitive. Applications to injection-molding pressure profiles and a nuisance-matched hydraulic benchmark illustrate transition localization and interpretable within-cycle diagnostics, while highlighting the need for dependence-aware calibration in naturally ordered industrial data.

papers.title: The out-state of scalar-induced gravitational waves
papers.summary: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) are described by second-order tensor perturbations that contain free radiation together with a gauge-dependent response maintained by the scalar source. For a perfect fluid with constant equation of state $0<w<1$, we identify the free radiation with the out-state of the tensor perturbation, assembled from the light-cone residue of kernel functions for each pair of scalar modes. Its amplitudes follow from a classical LSZ-type reduction formula, in terms of the initial data and the light-cone-projected source. We prove a classical equivalence theorem: a redefinition of the tensor perturbation whose late-time shift has power-law envelopes and no tensor-frequency component leaves these amplitudes unchanged. Transformations between intrinsic gauges, whose slice-normal observers and spatial coordinates are fixed by the matter and geometry without an external clock or independent oscillatory dynamics, are redefinitions of this kind, except on resonance surfaces of zero measure. The out-state is therefore the same in all intrinsic gauges, including the standard gauges of cosmological perturbation theory. The late-time Newtonian kernel is then the out-state kernel, which justifies its use for the energy spectrum of the free radiation. In matter domination, the out-state instead separates the free radiation from the static tidal response.

papers.title: Sufficient Dimension Reduction with Multimodal Predictor Objects
papers.summary: We study the regression of a scalar response $Y$ on a Euclidean predictor $\mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{R}^p$ and a random predictor object $\mathcal{Z}$ in a general metric space under arbitrary structural dependence. We introduce a joint sufficient dimension reduction $(\mathbf{B}^\top\mathbf{X}, \mathcal{G}_Z)$ constructed via a sequential conditional independence framework, which differs fundamentally from the ordinary central subspace of $Y \mid \mathbf{X}$. Methodologically, $\mathcal{Z}$ is embedded into a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, and a regularized kernel-response envelope model extracts a finite-dimensional reduction of the feature map. Partial adaptive estimation then recovers the Euclidean reduction conditional on the first-stage coordinates. We establish root-$n$ consistency rates for the first-stage envelope subspace under a shrinking regularizer, alongside large-sample consistency for the second-stage Euclidean subspace estimator. Simulations and two real-data applications illustrate the utility and flexibility of the proposed method.

papers.title: When Reasoning looks like Hidden Understanding: How Chain-of-Thought Fosters Anthropomorphism, Perceptions of Epistemic Superiority, and Cognitive Deference
papers.summary: As AI-based products permeate society, specifically systems using generative models, a belief system is emerging about what these products are and what they can and cannot do. One common belief concerns the perception of the form of language as evidence of 'understanding' language. As these generative models reproduce linguistic patterns rather than understand meaning, interpreting these patterns as evidence of understanding is a misattribution. This misconception is extended by the notion that generative models can 'explain their reasoning.' Anecdotally, these misconceptions which mistake the form of language for its meaning are driving cognitive deference to AI systems in a way that displaces human agency. Such mistakes involve attributions of cognitive properties to the system, allowing them to be treated like intentional 'minds'. Importantly, perceived epistemic authority and superiority make that 'mind' worth deferring to. Anthropomorphism in tandem with epistemic authority and superiority, we argue, increases the risk that users generalise from narrow task performance to broader competencies, committing the "fallacy of composition". This paper explores misconceptions of Chain of Thought (CoT) reasoning as sufficient transparent 'explanation'. We explore how anthropomorphism acts as a vehicle for cognitive deference of decision-making and perceptions of epistemic superiority in AI systems. Finally, we explore CoT's ramifications using medicine as an example. Taken together, we conclude that explainability operationalised through CoT is highly problematic and undercuts the very ethical principles it is intended to serve. While CoT may be valuable for improving output accuracy and moderation, we suggest that the practice of asking models to provide user facing reasons for their outputs should be actively discouraged, and AI literacy training should explicitly caution against its use.
papers.comment: Conference submission to FAccT, 4th November 2026. No Figures

papers.title: Economics of Selection in Ranking & Selection: Neither Fixed-Precision nor Fixed-Budget
papers.summary: Ranking and selection (R&S) has evolved tremendously over the last several decades, with applications in agriculture, discrete optimization with computer simulation, clinical trial design, and other areas. We challenge a widely accepted classification of R&S procedures into two categories: fixed-precision and fixed-budget. We discuss a third class, economics-of-selection (EoS) procedures, which is conceptually distinct and is found in the extant literature on Bayesian hypothesis testing and simulation optimization. Procedures in this third class seek to optimally balance two quantities: the cost of learning about the performance of each alternative and the quality of the alternative ultimately selected on the basis of that learning. Fixed-precision and fixed-budget procedures tend to optimize one of these quantities while constraining the other. We clarify these differences and show why they matter. We then present new frequentist R&S procedures in this third category, including both two-stage procedures and a sequential heuristic, assuming Gaussian observations with either known or unknown variances. We find that EoS is not a question of Bayesian versus frequentist analysis, asymptotic versus finite-sample analysis, finite-stage versus fully sequential procedures, or comparing one mean with a standard versus comparing multiple alternatives. We identify opportunities for further R&S research.

papers.title: Feedback Design in the Shadow of Strategic Communication
papers.summary: We study optimal feedback design when evaluations affect subsequent strategic communication within organizations. A firm designs public feedback about an employee's potential before the employee communicates private information about project-specific circumstances to a manager. While more informative feedback helps the manager make better decisions, it can also intensify preference conflicts and undermine the credibility of subsequent communication. We characterize the optimal feedback policy. First, full disclosure is either optimal for all prior beliefs or strictly suboptimal for all of them. In particular, it is optimal when preference conflicts are sufficiently small or sufficiently large. Second, when full disclosure is suboptimal, no disclosure is optimal for some priors, while partial disclosure is strictly optimal for some priors if and only if the number of messages in equilibrium communication varies with posterior beliefs. Third, optimal partial disclosure can conclusively identify low-potential employees when high potential is rare, but high-potential employees when it is common.

papers.title: 5G CATS: 5G-Based Cryptographic Authorization Against Trafficking of Semiconductor Devices
papers.summary: Enforcing export controls on AI accelerators requires verifying where a chip operates after deployment. Round-trip time measurements can bound a chip's distance from a trusted landmark, but any jitter in honest replies forces the verifier to loosen its timeout, giving an attacker slack to relay traffic over fiber from a restricted region. Prior approaches either cross the untrusted host stack or rely on noisy power-line channels that inflate this slack. We present 5G CATS, a location certification system that pairs a co-packaged 5G radio, cryptographic engine, and hardware interlock on the GPU package with 5G Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communication (URLLC) base stations. Terminating the radio link inside the package removes the host software, PCIe fabric, and baseboard management controller from the verification path. We map an authenticated challenge-response protocol onto 5G's slot structure, replace permanent key erasure with short-lived execution leases, and specify a cross-check of the chip's reported serving cell against the carrier's own attachment records. In ns-3 and 5G-LENA simulations of an unloaded cell, our URLLC-based radio profile narrows the 99.9th percentile round-trip spread to 2.60 ms, more than ten times narrower than default 5G. A tracer rejects every round of a fiber relay from 300 km, against 2,000 km for default 5G. Against a 3,000 km attacker, a tracer stays safe at up to 1,410 km from the chip, against at most 619 km for PowerCATS's published model, while default 5G is never safe.

papers.title: Regression Modeling for the Bloc Basu Bivariate Exponential Distribution: Marginal and Conditional Means
papers.summary: The bivariate absolutely continuous exponential distribution introduced by \citet{block1974continuous} provides a model for dependent lifetimes in reliability and survival analysis. Its marginal means depend jointly and nonlinearly on the rate parameters, which complicates regression modeling and the interpretation of covariate effects on these means. In this paper, we develop two regression approaches based on a region-wise multivariate exponential-family representation. In the full-distribution approach, link functions relate the cumulant derivatives in a fixed reference region to linear predictors. These derivatives do not directly equal the marginal means, which are instead probability-weighted combinations of the regional derivatives. This relationship allows covariate effects on the marginal means to be examined. Likelihood derivatives are obtained through the chain rule, and the regression coefficients are estimated by maximum likelihood. The rate parameter estimates are then recovered through the inverse link functions and an explicit inverse mapping, with the admissible solution selected to ensure positive rates. As an alternative, we propose regression models based on the normalized conditional distribution within each region. In this setting, the cumulant derivatives coincide with the conditional means, allowing covariates to be linked directly to these means. Both approaches are evaluated through a simulation study.

papers.title: Reconciling District Prediction Markets and Seat-Count Buckets in U.S. Midterm Elections
papers.summary: The prediction market platform Kalshi offers individual markets for the winner in each U.S. congressional district and an aggregate market for the total number of Democratic House seats. We develop an applied statistical framework for reconciling these two market layers, since the aggregate seat count is determined by the collection of individual district outcomes. The framework combines a latent-Gaussian dependence structure with a log-odds adjustment to district probabilities and a power adjustment to aggregate seat-count probabilities, with parameters estimated by divergence minimization. Applied to a July 30, 2026 snapshot, the three-parameter primary model achieves close reconciliation, with forward and reverse KL divergences both approximately 0.0013, while yielding a positive latent national correlation, a negative district log-odds shift, and flattening of the aggregate target distribution. Daily analysis of 236 dates from January through August 2026 reveals two relatively stable periods separated by a spring transition period exhibiting substantial volatility in both parameter and divergence values. The framework provides a diagnostic approach for assessing cross-market consistency in hierarchically structured prediction or financial markets.

papers.title: High-Dimensional Nonsparse Regression under Covariate Shift via Importance-Weighted Partial Least Squares
papers.summary: This paper studies high-dimensional nonsparse regression when the data exhibit both strong predictor dependence and covariate shift. Many existing regression methods struggle with highly correlated predictors, while covariate shift can make components learned from source data less effective for target-domain prediction. To address these joint challenges, we develop an importance-weighted partial least squares (IWPLS) method that reweights source observations to reflect the target covariate distribution and extracts response-relevant components for coefficient estimation. The resulting estimator depends on weighted sample covariances, which generally lack the usual Wishart structure even when the target-domain covariates are Gaussian. We therefore combine a perturbation analysis of weighted PLS moments with an influence-function decomposition to establish consistency for the one- and multi-component estimators and asymptotic normality for the one-component estimator. Simulation studies and real-data analyses show that IWPLS outperforms the benchmark methods considered.

papers.title: A dual-moment framework toward unification of the four fundamental interactions
papers.summary: The unification of the four fundamental interactions remains one of the central open challenges in fundamental physics. Most existing unification scenarios rely on extra spatial dimensions, novel symmetry structures, or unobserved dynamical degrees of freedom. In this work, we construct a minimal phenomenological dual-moment framework rooted in primitive charges and motion-induced kinetic moments. Gravitational, electromagnetic, and strong interactions are coherently described within a unified inverse-square-law formalism. We postulate a universal coupling relation $T = Z/c^2$ that connects source-charge coupling coefficients and moment-mediated coupling coefficients across different interaction sectors. While the framework can formally accommodate weak-charge degrees of freedom, full quantitative computations for weak-interaction dynamics are deferred to future follow-up studies. The model reproduces established low-energy dynamical limits for planetary orbits, atomic systems, and heavy-quark hadrons, and predicts distinguishable corrections to light deflection by rapidly spinning compact objects. We further design three independent test schemes: improved torsion-balance measurements, a mass-current laboratory deflection experiment, and astronomical light-bending observations. Although laboratory measurements impose formidable technical challenges, astronomical observations of compact spinning objects offer promising avenues to constrain or falsify the proposed framework.
papers.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures, submitted to Physical Review D. A classical unified framework for four fundamental interactions, with gravitational lensing and torsion balance tests

papers.title: Coherent control of quadrupolar order in solid spin-1 systems:\ majorization bounds, orientation-indexed adiabatic inversion, and order lifetime
papers.summary: Tensor polarization $\Pzz=1-3p_0$ of spin-1 nuclei in dynamically polarized solid targets is limited, under a single spin temperature, to $\Pzz^{\rm eq}=2-\sqrt{4-3P^2}$ ($\Pzz\simeq0.20$ at vector polarization $P=0.5$). Radio-frequency (rf) semi-saturation of one quadrupolar Pake-doublet branch, with and without slow sample rotation, has reached $\Pzz\simeq0.36$. Using the first-order quadrupole Hamiltonian, spin temperatures of the Zeeman and alignment (quadrupolar-order) reservoirs, and single-transition operators, we analyze these manipulations. Five results follow. (i) Under unital operations (rf pulses, rotation, saturation), $1-3λ_{\max}\le\Pzz\le1-3λ_{\min}$, where $λ_{\min,\max}$ are the smallest and largest initial populations. Saturation achieves at most half the available transfer; selective $π$ inversion reaches either bound ($\Pzz=-0.85,+0.65$ at $P=0.5$). (ii) In a powder, the two single-quantum transitions overlap except in the pedestal region. Adiabatic frequency sweeps confined there invert one transition per bond. Inverting each bond exactly once requires packing antipodal caps on the orientation sphere. The optimal single-axis arrangement has four stops at the magic angle $54.74\degree$ (cube body diagonals; 73\% coverage); six icosahedral axes give the global optimum (90\%). (iii) Rotation-induced Landau--Zener crossings of deuteron pairs are adiabatic at current rates and scramble the inversion pattern; transits must be fast for the strongest, geminal CD$_2$, pairs. (iv) A parity theorem determines the inverted bonds solely from the endpoints of continuous adiabatic passage: rf during rotation yields at most two caps, and a full turn none. (v) The enhanced state decays by dipolar flip-flops, with $T_{1Q}\le T_{1Z}/3$ and a duty-cycle break-even of $\simeq35$~min. Magic-angle spinning cannot replace this scheme.

papers.title: Stinging the Swarm: Extracting Attacker Intelligence from a Twin-Controller OT Honeypot
papers.summary: Autonomous language-model agents can drive industrial controllers over fieldbus protocols, probing a plant at machine speed and in coordinated swarms. We present Talos, an inline gate that judges every agent request to a controller in milliseconds and routes agents it flags as hostile to a device-faithful decoy -- a mirror twin of the real plant -- where their attack continues harmlessly and is read for intelligence. We evaluate the full pipeline (detect -> quarantine -> mirror -> extract) against 2,400 autonomous attacker agents, 600 in each of four tiers that escalate the attacker's effort to stay hidden, from no concealment to an explicit non-disclosure rule and a trained cover story. No write reached the real plant in any tier: the gate denies the damage path and a device-level envelope check backstops it, while unmapped registers are denied without exception and the gate still permits safe-direction stop commands. Decisions are model-driven in every tier with no inference timeouts, closing a common objection to small on-device judges. Beyond blocking, the pipeline reads the attacker. We find a behavioral structure along two axes -- how persistently an agent attacks and how much it discloses -- and show that the system has a capture channel for three of the four resulting regions: hardened, silent attackers escalate most and are read on the mirror; compliant, talkative attackers volunteer their identity to a diagnostic form before they are ever quarantined; only the paranoid, low-yield region resists both. Attacker identity fields are self-authored cover stories, but involuntary tells -- the self-reported toolchain fingerprint and the attacker's own list of targeted registers -- accumulate across the swarm into a high-confidence profile drawn from agents under explicit orders to stay silent. The gate, mirror, and harness are released under Apache 2.0 with a synthetic device family.

papers.title: Thermal $CP$ dynamics in a four-fermion model: mean-field and functional renormalization group analyses
papers.summary: We investigate a one-flavor four-fermion model with scalar, pseudoscalar, and mixed scalar-pseudoscalar interactions at finite temperature and vanishing chemical potential. Our analysis combines the mean-field approximation, which determines the equilibrium condensates, with the functional renormalization group (FRG), which describes the scale dependence of the interactions and the fermion mass phase. Within the mean-field approach, we find that, in the absence of explicit symmetry-breaking sources, the dominant interaction determines the direction of condensation. In particular, a pseudoscalar condensate spontaneously breaks the ordinary $P/CP$ symmetry and disappears through a continuous thermal phase transition. For regular high-temperature FRG trajectories, the dimensionless mixed coupling tends to zero in the infrared, while its dimensionful counterpart remains finite. Increasing temperature also suppresses the scale evolution of the fermion mass phase. Together, these results clarify the distinct roles of thermal fluctuations in suppressing spontaneous symmetry breaking and fermionic instabilities, without necessarily eliminating explicit symmetry breaking effects.

papers.title: Orthographic depth at two scales, with English also matched for lexicon size
papers.summary: A reader can struggle to read in only one of their languages, and one proposed reason is how predictably spelling maps to sound. We measure that predictability as conditional entropy, the pronunciation uncertainty left once the spelling is seen, at two grain sizes (unit sizes): the alignment unit, an aligned spelling-sound chunk, and the syllable, bounded in the pronunciation. We analyse word lists in twelve alphabetic orthographies and report five in full, with English pronunciations from a dictionary and the rest from the synthesizer eSpeak-ng, length marks removed. Among the five, English has the most uncertainty and Finnish the least at both grains. Across all twelve, Portuguese and Danish exceed English per alignment unit, and German and Italian order differently by grain and transcription. These orders hold when English is transcribed by eSpeak-ng with u allowed to spell /j/ plus a vowel. Uncertainty per unit has no shared direction as units grow: it falls in Spanish and, less securely, German, is level in Finnish, depends on transcription in Italian and on the word list in English, and rises in Norwegian and Swedish. Summed uncertainty per word falls in all twelve, but that score is handed the pronunciation's boundaries and mixes context with in-sample memorisation, so it is no evidence of what a reader computes. An exact identity states when discarded spelling boundaries could reverse that fall. A uniform 20,000-word English sample holds 35% of the dictionary's syllable spellings and has syllable entropy 0.098 bits lower, so lexicons must be matched in size. In an exploratory check over eleven languages, syllable-scale entropy tracked first-year reading accuracy (rho = -0.74, falling to -0.25 if English is given the lowest entropy instead), without separating the syllable scale from the alignment unit. These estimates describe sampled writing systems, not readers.
papers.comment: 38 pages, 5 figures. Spelling-to-sound entropy as a measure of orthographic depth for cross-language reading research; exploratory check against Grade 1 reading accuracy in Section 3.5. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/A9T3C

papers.title: The Dose Makes the Poison: Exposure-Aware Evaluation of Generative Drug Design
papers.summary: Generative models are increasingly used to propose molecules for drug discovery. They can produce far more candidates than can be experimentally tested, making computational selection essential. Most selection methods rely on predicted molecular properties, such as potency and toxicity, but overlook how these properties translate into drug exposure at a given dose. As a result, molecules that appear promising on paper may require impractical doses or raise safety concerns. We investigate this gap by using physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) simulations to re-evaluate molecules selected from three PARP1-targeted generative pipelines. Of 60 shortlisted molecules, seven fail to achieve sufficient target exposure, while 28% of the remaining candidates show predicted safety risks at their required dose. Moreover, 85% of candidates with an achievable dose are outperformed by molecules overlooked during static selection. These findings suggest that accounting for dose and exposure can substantially change which generated molecules are considered promising for drug development.
papers.comment: 14 pages, 3 figures. Accepted at the AI4DD workshop (AI for Drug Discovery: Bridging the Translation Gap), NeurIPS 2026

papers.title: Towards Accessible, Autonomous Photosynthesis Monitoring on Living Leaves
papers.summary: Photosynthesis is a direct biomarker of plant health and functioning. However, measuring net photosynthesis on individual leaves requires expensive (USD 42,000 - USD 89,000) instruments and manual effort. This limits access to photosynthesis sensing and makes long-term monitoring across multiple leaves difficult. We present a 1000x low-cost, autonomous sensing system that enables longitudinal monitoring of photosynthesis on living leaves over multiple days. Guided by a formative user study with 13 plant biology researchers, the system integrates an automated, leaf-attached chamber with a low-cost CO2 sensor. Built using a 3D-printed clamp and thermoformed dome, the chamber periodically closes to measure CO2 drawdown and reopens to refresh the air. Each chamber costs about USD 62 and operates independently, allowing multiple leaves to be monitored simultaneously without pumps or gas tubing. We characterize each chamber and validate its measurements against a research-grade gas exchange instrument (CIRAS-4) across 29 sessions (R^2 = 0.90). We also demonstrate monitoring of C3 and CAM photosynthesis plants, adaptability to different leaf geometries, and a light-response experiment. In a nine-day deployment, six chambers captured simultaneous CO2 exchange from individual leaves of the same plant during drought and rewatering. Each leaf showed different patterns of nighttime CO2 uptake and recovery, which a whole-plant CO2 measurement instrument would obscure. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of such leaf-level photosynthesis dynamics using independent, low-cost autonomous chambers. Our work opens new opportunities for plant science, education, and data-driven agriculture.

papers.title: Designing Accessible and Rigorous ML Experiments: No-Code Visual Workflows and Structured Guidance for Beginners
papers.summary: Designing machine learning (ML) experiments requires beginners to plan a methodologically sound workflow and implement it in a concrete environment. We evaluated two forms of support in two within-participant studies with 18 predominantly technically trained participants: mlguide, which provides structured, evidence- backed guidance for workflow design, and AI Sandbox, a visual no-code environment for workflow implementation. After using mlguide, participants produced better high-level workflow designs, but their scores on a quiz about specific methodological choices did not improve significantly. Compared with Google Colab, AI Sandbox received higher hedonic user experience ratings, while perceived workload and acceptance did not differ significantly. These findings suggest that different forms of interactive support help with differ- ent aspects of beginner ML experimentation. The paper contributes a reusable evaluation task with instructions, a modified dataset, and a quiz, as well as empirical evidence on structured guidance for workflow design and on the experience of implementing workflows in visual and notebook-based environments.

papers.title: Quantifying the impact of 3D diffusion and local versus global removal by surface deposition on indoor airborne transmission
papers.summary: The Viral Infection Risk Indoor Simulator (VIRIS) [Xue et al. 2024] combines architectural layout, people movement, and airborne transmission modelling to predict infection risk in indoor spaces. The modelling assumptions in VIRIS include: (i) uniform aerosol concentration over the building height, allowing airborne transmission to be modelled in a two-dimensional (2D) domain, and (ii) first-order global removal of aerosols to account for surface deposition. Both assumptions lead to underestimating the infectious aerosol concentration in the breathing zone. Here, we extend VIRIS to model airborne transmission more realistically and compare the impact on infection risk predictions. We develop VIRIS-3D-L by extending the airborne transmission model in VIRIS (a reaction-diffusion equation) to three dimensions (3D) and replacing global removal with a Robin boundary condition representing localised removal due to surface deposition. We compare VIRIS and VIRIS-3D-L across three single-storey buildings with increasing architectural and people-movement complexity: a courtroom, a care home, and a supermarket. We find that VIRIS underestimates the disease transmission rate and infection risks for individuals by up to 50% relative to VIRIS-3D-L in all three buildings. However, VIRIS-3D-L requires, on average, four times the computation time of VIRIS, mainly because it extends the computational domain from a 2D surface to a 3D volume. Overall, VIRIS-3D-L provides a more realistic modelling of airborne transmission than VIRIS and is particularly suited to settings with variations in people and furniture heights and frequent 3D movement. For simpler single-storey buildings, VIRIS is suitable because of its lower computational cost.

papers.title: Ender: Visual Scaffolding for Geometric Proof Comprehension
papers.summary: Geometric proof is a foundational but notoriously difficult topic in secondary mathematics, primarily due to the high cognitive load required to integrate visual diagrams with logical text. As proofs evolve, tracking the initial givens and an expanding set of derived truths can easily overwhelm working memory. While established scaffolding techniques are often visual and diagram-based, current digital learning environments mostly rely on static, text-heavy interfaces that force students to manage these complex mental models on their own. This paper introduces Ender, an interactive rendering system designed to visualize the logical status of two-column proofs. Ender's design is grounded in four literature-derived requirements: (1) diagram annotation, (2) structural tracing, (3) support for partial or incorrect work, and (4) synchronization between the diagram and text. To evaluate the system, we conducted a between-subjects, think-aloud experiment with 12 secondary school students in the United States, comparing Ender against a traditional digital proof interface. Our results indicate that students using Ender performed significantly better on proof comprehension tasks--specifically in identifying and correcting logical errors. These findings suggest that dynamic visual scaffolding may ease the working memory burden of digital interfaces, offering a promising building block for future AI-based proof tutoring systems.

papers.title: No finite rulebook can certify every safe program: an impossibility theorem for gatekeeping AI agents
papers.summary: An AI assistant writes small programs, and a gatekeeper must decide, from the code alone, whether each one may run. Suppose the rules are fixed: never perform a forbidden action, never let the output depend on a secret, always answer eventually. Can two rulebooks, one listing what is allowed and one listing what is not, both be complete, if every rule must be backed by evidence that a machine can check in finite time? We prove that they cannot. Checkable evidence can only establish what a finite record settles, and ``never'' and ``eventually'' are never settled by a finite record. For prohibitions the failure is one-sided: every violation can be caught by watching, but no safe program can be cleared for good. For confidentiality and responsiveness, neither side can be. We characterise exactly which rules about visible behaviour evidence can confirm, and we show that any sound rulebook of $n$ bits omits a compliant program of about $n$ bits. A time limit makes everything checkable, but only by running the program for essentially the whole limit, so a finite machine is not a feasible one. Finally, we show what a gatekeeper can still guarantee: not a verdict on every program, but a checkable list that contains everything it must allow and nothing it must refuse. Simulations on 2.2 million random programs and on self-referential adversaries show that the obstruction is adversarial rather than typical, and that the one error a longer test never removes is the liveness part of confidentiality.

papers.title: Making sense of rule 605
papers.summary: The paper analyzes monthly reports of two companies: one market maker, Virtu, and one broker-dealer, SoHo, in the period between January 2021 and March 2024. The predictive power of standard methods for the probability laws of stock orders- linear regression and LSTM- is poor, despite their probability laws being relatively stable. However, the month-to-month correlations are highly stable and predictable. In this paper, we study the distributions of the sixteen datasets resulting from the 26 stock-trading parameters reported by brokerages under regulatory requirements.
papers.comment: First version of the manuscript. Comments welcome

papers.title: ProTEUS: A mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution
papers.summary: Protein engineering requires navigating rugged fitness landscapes, where small sequence changes can produce large functional differences, but experimental screening can only sample a small fraction of sequence space. Thus, a central challenge is to efficiently traverse the large combinatorial space of mutations in silico. We introduce ProTEUS, a mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution. Pretrained on deep mutational scanning assays, ProTEUS learns a joint representation of sequence, evolutionary, and structural information using MutationFormer, a mutation-biased attention architecture. Variants are represented as states in this joint latent space, and mutations define actions whose functional consequences are predicted. To support exploration of many mutants, we developed a fast, physics-constrained all-atom predictor that utilizes explicit geometric constraint enforcement to achieve >10 fold increase in speed than AlphaFold3 with guaranteed physical validity. Lastly, ProTEUS refines its prediction and understanding of protein activity through closed loop experimental feedback to guide evolution toward a desired phenotype. ProTEUS surpasses established models in both zero-shot and supervised fine-tuning mutation prediction tasks. We experimentally demonstrate its utility in two closed-loop multi-objective engineering campaigns on aldehyde dehydrogenase and levansucrase, yielding variants with >10 fold higher activity than wild type. ProTEUS provides a world-model framework that connects virtual evaluation of mutational outcomes with experimental learning for efficient protein evolution.

papers.title: Early Rug Pull Detection on Solana
papers.summary: Web3 platforms that help users discover and trade newly launched crypto tokens, including launchpads, decentralized-exchange (DEX) interfaces, wallets, and token-analytics sites, must assess tokens before their legitimacy is clear. On Solana, where token creation is inexpensive and tokens use standard programs rather than custom per-token smart contracts, rug pulls can unfold within minutes. Effective warnings must therefore rely on limited histories. Although graph neural networks (GNNs) have improved rug-pull detection on EVM chains, it remains unclear whether transfer structure adds predictive value over non-graph models at minute-scale decision points, and how that value changes as history accumulates. We study 2,700 tokens sampled from SolRPDS, collecting one-minute market histories from Birdeye and token transfers from Solana RPC. We define a rug pull operationally by requiring a liquidity drain, price collapse, and persistent liquidity depletion over a nominal 24-hour period after token creation. All features use only information available at or before each prediction cutoff. We evaluate observation windows of 12.5, 35.5, and 93 minutes, selected in advance from the published lifespan distribution of Solana rug pulls, and represent each token as a temporal transfer graph. Within the first 12.5 minutes, rug-pull and non-rug graphs already differ in size, density, reciprocity, and receiver-side centralization. We compare GNNs against matched non-graph models using the same token-level and graph-summary features on identical samples. A fixed panel of tokens observed in all three windows further isolates the effect of longer observation from changes in token population. Our findings inform the design of early-warning mechanisms for newly launched Solana tokens in Web3 interfaces.

papers.title: Veritas: A Verifier Generation Harness for Agent Tasks
papers.summary: The effectiveness of a self-improving system relies heavily on the quality of its verifier, which judges the outcome of each improvement round. However, the verifiers of most tasks are written by hand, which is expensive and does not scale to tasks that come without one. We propose Veritas, a harness that generates verifiers automatically. Unlike general-purpose agent harnesses, Veritas adds three mechanisms for verifier generation: an evidence header stating what the verifier will observe, a library of domain rules that tasks leave unstated, and authoring principles, partly refined by a self-improvement loop. We evaluate on six benchmarks: four scored by execution, whose official verifiers we first certify, and two that compare pairs of responses. With the model fixed, the verifiers Veritas generates agree better with the official verdicts than those of seven other harnesses on all four execution-scored benchmarks. On the two pairwise benchmarks they are at or near the best. They also agree better than those of the vendor's own harness for two of three other model families. Its mechanisms also improve 9 of 12 harness-benchmark pairs scored by execution across three harnesses.

papers.title: Causal mediation analysis for a time-to-event endpoint in the presence of competing events
papers.summary: Causal mediation analysis is widely used to decompose a treatment's effect into components operating through distinct causal pathways and to characterize the mediator--outcome relationship. In time-to-event settings, competing events --- events that preclude the primary endpoint --- substantially complicate this decomposition. We provide a unified treatment of causal mediation analysis for a time-to-event endpoint under competing events. We show that the total effect on the cause-specific cumulative incidence decomposes into a direct effect, an indirect effect through the mediator of interest, and an indirect effect through the competing events. We develop this decomposition under the natural effects, stochastic interventional effects, and separable effects frameworks, and show that, in certain settings, all three yield identical statistical functionals despite relying on distinct identification assumptions. We derive efficient influence functions for the counterfactual cumulative incidence curves and the decomposed effects, and propose double-machine-learning-type estimators that are multiply robust and attain the semiparametric efficiency bound, with a sensitivity analysis to address unmeasured common causes of time-to-event endpoints. We further study the mediator--outcome response relationship via kernel-smoothed estimands. We apply the methods to immune correlates analyses of COVID-19 vaccine and HIV-1 prevention trials.

papers.title: MicroLens: Read, Trace, and Rewire the Residual Stream with Two Lenses
papers.summary: Lenses that decode hidden states into words are a popular way to look inside language models, but a heatmap of decoded words only shows what a vector reads as and cannot distinguish whether, or how much, the model uses the information. We present an interactive viewer that puts reading, tracing and editing on the same layers-by-tokens grid of the residual stream. In the viewer, every cell can be decoded with two lenses, the logit lens and the Jacobian lens (J-lens), traced back to the tokens it drew from, and edited, with the rest of the model rerun on the spot. We demonstrate three usage scenarios on Gemma-3-4B-it, backed by sweeps over a few hundred prompts, to show what this tool can discover. First, the two lenses give different directions to write with, each suiting a different edit: the logit lens's word direction sets what a token outputs, while the J-lens's direction changes what later tokens read. Second, in two-hop trivia questions (the capital of the state or country containing a given city), the state or country is readable at the city token from as early as layer 7, and swapping it there can redirect the answer 92-98% of the time; however, at the answer position, the state or country information is not used. Third, when a chat model answers questions with a step-by-step reasoning prompt, the correct answer is often already the top word in the residual stream before any reasoning is written: for 89-92% of retrieval questions and 39-63% of multi-hop and serial ones, far above their respective distractors (at most 5%). However, ordering puzzles are an exception, as the model works them out only once it writes its final reasoning steps. Furthermore, for answers that are visible in the residual stream, the J-lens reads them a layer or two earlier than the logit lens across the different types of question.

papers.title: Instrumental variables with treatment clusters
papers.summary: Many policy evaluations include multiple unordered treatments. A common approach is to aggregate these treatments into clusters and apply instrumental variable (IV) methods at the treatment cluster level: The clusters are treated as binary treatments and the IV assumptions are invoked at the cluster level. This paper shows that IV with treatment clusters identifies a weighted average of local average treatment effects (LATEs) under a set of assumptions at the unclustered treatment level. When data on unclustered treatment choice is available, we propose testable necessary conditions for the causal interpretation of IV with treatment clusters. We illustrate our methods with empirical applications to the causal effects of fields of study aggregated into STEM and non-STEM clusters or eight broad study directions.

papers.title: Does Haptic Connection to a Healthy Partner Improve Motor Learning in Chronic Stroke? A Pilot Study of Robot-Based Dyadic Training
papers.summary: Purpose: Robot-based haptic dyads, where two users exchange forces through robots, have been proposed for robot-assisted neurorehabilitation. This intervention could increase motor learning by promoting motor variability, providing an implicit communication channel, and facilitating social interaction. Despite the potential benefits, few studies have investigated robot-based haptic dyads for neurological populations, and none have included a comprehensive clinical assessment. Design/Methodology/Approach: We present a pilot study investigation of individuals with chronic stroke learning a complex tracking task in solo and dyad conditions. Prior to training, participants completed a battery of cognitive, motor, and sensory assessments. We assessed changes in key kinematic outcomes including tracking error, distance traveled, mean absolute power, and sample entropy. We also performed a correlation analysis of clinical scores with baseline tracking errors. Findings: Baseline tracking error was strongly correlated (r > 0.6) with lower cognitive scores and higher motor scores. Only the solo group demonstrated lower tracking error at assessment (Δ = -5.33, 95%CI [-10.25, -0.40], p = 0.027), but this result was tempered by the removal of an outlier participant. Neither group demonstrated clear retention. The dyad group showed significantly elevated performance, effort, and movement complexity during training. Research Limitations/Implications: The selected task was too difficult to reveal learning for either group, which may be related to its high cognitive demand. Sample size and stroke heterogeneity were also limitation. Originality/Value: Dyadic training increased movement complexity and effort, which are associated with better motor learning. Clinical characteristics such as lesion location, cognition, sensation, and chronicity may influence potential benefits of dyadic training.

papers.title: Time Series Change Point Detection with Gaussian Processes
papers.summary: This paper proposes a novel general Gaussian process framework for change point detection in time series. A change is defined as an alteration of the hyperparameters of the Gaussian process prior. We formulate the problem in the context of statistical hypothesis testing and demonstrate its performance over both offline and online multiple change points detection. The approach provides theoretical guaranties of its performance. An important advantage of the developed framework is that it does not need a detailed specification of the time series function before and after a change. The hyperparameter values are learned from the data. Comprehensive evaluation of the proposed framework is provided both on synthetic and real data and its efficiency is demonstrated.

papers.title: Project Progress Desk: Know Where All Your Claude Code and Codex Projects Stand at a Glance
papers.summary: Codex and Claude Code let developers work on many projects in parallel, but keeping track of them still means switching between chats, terminal sessions and providers. We present Project Progress Desk, a local desktop interface that brings overall progress, blockers and pending decisions into one view. Users can see which projects need attention, inspect what remains, and compare earlier approaches before choosing how to continue. Agent receipts link reported outcomes to each project's weighted acceptance checklist; the overview distinguishes receipt-supported progress from dated estimates. We describe daily use across 36 projects, including a choice between two implementations based on their recorded outcomes. At the demo, attendees will explore 30 simulated projects, trace completed work to overall progress, and watch a coding agent's new result update the overview.
papers.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures. Submitted to IUI 2027 Demos

papers.title: Viscosity heats, diffusion drains: Open-system thermodynamics in unimodular cosmology
papers.summary: In GR with bulk viscosity and in unimodular gravity with energy diffusion, the matter sector is non-adiabatic, and their balance, entropy, and temperature equations match if $Π\leftrightarrow \dot{Q}/3H$. Disagreement over whether unimodular cosmology is adiabatic comes from assigning entropy to matter only or to the total effective fluid.
